signals.title: Heap-use-after-free: Parquet v3 prefetcher reads and writes through a `ReadBuffer` freed by `IInputFormat::onFinish`
signals.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong `ParquetV3BlockInputFormat` does not override `resetReadBuffer()`, so `IInputFormat::onFinish()` frees the format's owned `ReadBuffer` while the Parquet `Prefetcher`'s IO tasks are still reading through it on the prefetch thread pool. The tasks then dereference freed memory. ASan on a plain `clickhouse local` run of the reproducer below (master, 26.8.1.1310): ``` ==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x7112bd001800 WRITE of size 1048576 at 0x7112bd001800 thread T9 (ParquetPrefetch) #3 in DB::ReadBuffer::next() src/IO/ReadBuffer.cpp:113:15 #5 in DB::ReadBuffer::read(char*, unsigned long) src/IO/ReadBuffer.h:169:37 #6 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::readSync(...) src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Prefetcher.cpp:113:29 #7 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::runTask(...) src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Prefetcher.cpp:540:13 #8 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::scheduleTask(...)::$_0::operator()() src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Prefetcher.cpp:435 #15 in DB::ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerFast::threadFunction() src/Common/threadPoolCallbackRunner.cpp:225:13 ``` It is a **1 MiB write into freed heap**, so this is memory corruption, not only a bad read. The same defect was hit independently by the `La Casa Del Dolor (arm_asan_ubsan)` CI job, where the report is a read and carries the full free/allocation stacks: ``` ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0xfcdd2aec39c0 READ of size 8 at 0xfcdd2aec39c0 thread T423 (ThreadPool) #0 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::readSync(...) Prefetcher.cpp:110:21 <- reader->setReadUntilEnd() #1 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::runTask(...) Prefetcher.cpp:523:13 #2 in DB::Parquet::Prefetcher::scheduleTask(...)::$_0::operator()() Prefetcher.cpp:424:17 #9 in DB::ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerFast::threadFunction() threadPoolCallbackRunner.cpp:225:13 0xfcdd2aec39c0 is located 0 bytes inside of 272-byte region freed by thread T468 (ThreadPool) here: #1 in std::default_delete<DB::ReadBuffer>::operator()(DB::ReadBuffer*) #7 in std::vector<std::unique_ptr<DB::ReadBuffer>>::~vector() #8 in DB::ISource::work() src/Processors/ISource.cpp:140:13 ... #18 in DB::IPolygonDictionary::loadData() src/Dictionaries/PolygonDictionary.cpp:337:8 previously allocated by thread T468 (ThreadPool) here: #2 in DB::FileDictionarySource::loadAll() src/Dictionaries/FileDictionarySource.cpp:60:19 ``` `ISource.cpp:140` is the `onFinish()` call inside the `catch (...)` handler, and the freed 272-byte region is the `ReadBufferFromFile` that `FileDictionarySource::loadAll` handed to the format via `addBuffer`. ## How to reproduce Reproduces on master (26.8.1.1310) with the official `build_amd_asan_ubsan` binary, **8 out of 10 runs, with no ThreadFuzzer and no unusual settings**. Under ThreadFuzzer it hit on the first run. Run Fiddle: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/06f26a34-d286-40a1-85f5-7d3e952d47b8 On a release build this prints only the load error and exits 53: `Code: 53. CAST AS Array can only be performed between same-dimensional Array ... While executing ParquetV3BlockInputFormat. (TYPE_MISMATCH)` — the 1 MiB write into freed memory is silent. On an ASan build the process dies with the report above instead (5/5 runs of exactly the commands above; 8/10 in an earlier variant, so it is a race, but a very wide one). The polygon dictionary is only a convenient way to make the pipeline throw mid-read while owning its `ReadBuffer` — the defect is in the format, not in the dictionary. ## Root cause `Prefetcher` protects only *its own* lifetime. `scheduleTask` captures the shutdown handle and each task takes `std::shared_lock(*_shutdown, std::try_to_lock)`; `~Prefetcher` calls `shutdown->shutdown()` (`ShutdownHelper`, `src/Common/threadPoolCallbackRunner.h:507`), which blocks until every in-flight task has released. As its own comment says, "`this` is safe to access as long as `shutdown_lock` is held". But `Prefetcher::reader` points at a `ReadBuffer` owned by `IInputFormat::owned_buffers`, an unrelated lifetime that the handshake does not cover: - `IInputFormat::onFinish()` -> `resetReadBuffer()` -> `resetOwnedBuffers()` -> `owned_buffers.clear()` - `ParquetV3BlockInputFormat` overrides `resetParser()` and `onCancel()`, but **not `resetReadBuffer()`**. `resetParser()` happens to be safe only because it destroys the reader *before* delegating to the base. `resetReadBuffer()` has no such ordering, so the buffer dies while the `ReadManager` -> `Reader` -> `Prefetcher` chain is still alive with tasks running. Three routes reach it: `onFinish()` from the `catch (...)` in `ISource::work()` (the one above), `onFinish()` on the normal completion path (`ISource.cpp:133`) with speculative prefetches still outstanding, and `IInputFormat::setReadBuffer` when a format is reused across files. ## Suggested fix Mirror what `resetParser()` already does, so `~Prefetcher` drains the IO tasks before the base frees the buffer: ```cpp void ParquetV3BlockInputFormat::resetReadBuffer() { /// ~Prefetcher waits for in-flight IO tasks, which read through the buffer that /// IInputFormat::resetReadBuffer() is about to free. { std::lock_guard lock(reader_mutex); reader.reset(); } IInputFormat::resetReadBuffer(); } ``` ## Additional context Distinct from #109678 / #112573. That was a data race on `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::prefetch_future` consumed by concurrent `readBigAt` (the `RandomRead` branch, `Prefetcher.cpp:102`). This one is a lifetime bug in the `SeekAndRead` branch, which already holds `read_mutex` — locking cannot help once the object is freed — and the freed buffer here is a plain `ReadBufferFromFile`, so `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer` is not involved at all. The binary used above already contains #112573 (merged into 26.8.1.1240). Found by this Dolor run: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=a2ef409981fc77a168eaf8cc68d7ddf67c9fadec&name_0=PR&name_1=La+Casa+Del+Dolor+%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114668 - Backported to: `26.7.4.42`, `26.5.7.56`, `26.3.18.30` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: KeyCondition's pointInPolygon primary-key analysis skips is_valid validation (unlike pointInPolygon/spatial_bbox/GeoParquet pruning)
signals.text: ### Describe the unexpected behaviour `KeyCondition`'s primary-key range analysis for `pointInPolygon` (`analyze_point_in_polygon` in `src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp:3583-3663`) builds the query polygon directly from the literal argument, calls `boost::geometry::correct` and `boost::geometry::envelope`, but never calls `boost::geometry::is_valid`. This is inconsistent with the other two places in the codebase that parse the same kind of literal: - `FunctionPointInPolygon::parseConstPolygon`/`parseConstMultiPolygon` (`src/Functions/pointInPolygon.cpp:842-861,894-913`), which validate the assembled polygon with `bg::is_valid` and throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when `validate_polygons` is enabled (the default). - The `spatial_bbox` `MergeTree` skip index and GeoParquet row-group pruning (`src/Common/GeoBbox.h`, added in #104437), which validate every constant geometry argument and fail closed (decline to prune) rather than derive a bbox from an invalid one. `analyze_point_in_polygon` also only recognizes the plain 2-argument `pointInPolygon(point, ring)` form (see the `Case1 no holes in polygon` comment at line 3715); a polygon-with-holes literal (3+ arguments) isn't analyzed for primary-key pruning at all. That part is safe (it just declines to prune, so `KeyCondition` falls back to scanning), it's the missing validity check on the single-ring case that's the actual gap. ### Practical impact Under the default `validate_polygons = 1`, this gap is effectively unreachable through SQL: ClickHouse evaluates `WHERE`-clause constant expressions once on a zero-row block before any index analysis or pruning runs, so an invalid constant polygon literal passed to `pointInPolygon` always raises `BAD_ARGUMENTS` immediately — `KeyCondition`'s analysis, which runs later during part/granule selection, never gets a chance to act on the unvalidated bbox. However, if a user explicitly sets `validate_polygons = 0` — a documented, supported way to bypass `pointInPolygon`'s own geometry validation — the dry-run exception no longer fires, and `KeyCondition`'s PK-range analysis still unconditionally computes a bbox/envelope from the same, now genuinely unvalidated, polygon and may use it to prune primary-key ranges. `boost::geometry`'s query algorithms (`within`, `intersects`, etc.) have undefined results for invalid geometries, so pruning decisions derived from such a polygon are not guaranteed to be sound. ### How to reproduce Not reproducible with a concrete wrong-result example yet — this is a code-review finding, not an observed bug. The scenario would require: a `MergeTree` table with a `pointInPolygon`-friendly primary key, `SETTINGS validate_polygons = 0`, and a self-intersecting/otherwise invalid constant polygon literal in the `WHERE` clause, compared against a full scan of the same query. ### Expected behavior `analyze_point_in_polygon` should either validate the polygon the same way `FunctionPointInPolygon` and `Common/GeoBbox.h` do (and fail closed / decline to prune when invalid, honoring `validate_polygons` the same way the function itself does), or the inconsistency should be a deliberate, documented decision. ### Additional context Found while auditing ClickHouse's geospatial pruning code for duplicated/drifted logic during #104437 (which unified the equivalent bbox-extraction-and-validation logic between the `spatial_bbox` skip index and GeoParquet row-group pruning in `src/Common/GeoBbox.h`). Filing this as a lower-priority follow-up for future reference rather than addressing it in that PR, since it's a different subsystem (primary-key range analysis) and not currently reachable under default settings. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114710 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1487` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Serial single-level to two-level conversion in aggregation merge prep regressed ClickBench Q10/Q11 2-3x on 192-core machines (exposed by #107490 memory accounting)
signals.text: Between the official ClickBench mainline runs of 2026-03-27 (≈26.3) and 2026-08-11 (latest stable, 26.7.x) on `c7a.metal-48xl` (192 vCPU), the `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` queries regressed while overall hot performance stayed flat (hot geomean 0.97): | query | hot 2026-03-27 | hot 2026-08-11 | ratio | |---|---|---|---| | Q10 `SELECT MobilePhoneModel, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits WHERE MobilePhoneModel <> '' GROUP BY MobilePhoneModel ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10` | 0.114 s | 0.196 s | **1.7x** | | Q11 `SELECT MobilePhone, MobilePhoneModel, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits WHERE MobilePhoneModel <> '' GROUP BY MobilePhone, MobilePhoneModel ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10` | 0.078 s | 0.257 s | **3.3x** | | Q37 (possibly related) | 0.023 s | 0.042 s | 1.8x | `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` maps to `uniqExact` by default (`count_distinct_implementation`), and the evidence points at `uniqExact` state merging at high thread counts specifically: - The versions benchmark (`c7a.4xlarge`, 16 vCPU) shows **no** regression on these queries across 26.3 → 26.7 → master — but it substitutes `uniq(UserID)` for `COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` (oldest-compatible query set), so it does not exercise `uniqExact` at all. - On a 96-core aarch64 box with the same 100M-row dataset, 26.7.1.1315 and current master both run Q10/Q11 in ~0.07 s hot — no regression at 96 threads. - So the degradation manifests only on the 192-vCPU machine, i.e. it scales badly with thread count rather than being a general codegen regression. Q10/Q11 have few groups (mobile phone models) with large per-group `uniqExact` states over ~100M rows — the merge of many per-thread large states is the hot path. A bisect of the 26.3 → 26.7 window on a high-core-count machine is needed; candidates are changes to parallel aggregation state merging or `uniqExact`-specific merge paths. Found while investigating the ClickBench dashboard delta for PR #81944 — this regression is unrelated to that PR but inflates the hot side of its dashboard comparison. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944#issuecomment-5280709772 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114691 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1469` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: The trivial GROUP BY LIMIT optimization returns wrong results with DISTINCT, QUALIFY, window functions or arrayJoin in the projection
signals.text: The trivial `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` optimization (`optimize_trivial_group_by_limit_query`, default `true` since 26.5) rewrites eligible queries to `max_rows_to_group_by = n + offset` with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'`, so the aggregation keeps only the first `n + offset` distinct keys. That is only sound when the LIMIT directly cuts the produced groups. The shape check misses four constructs that consume or filter the groups **between** the aggregation and the LIMIT, and each of them returns wrong results with default settings (verified on current master, top-level queries, multi-threaded): **`DISTINCT`** — collapses the projected groups before LIMIT. 100000 groups yield 4 distinct values, `LIMIT 3` must return 3 rows; with the rewrite the aggregation is cut at 3 keys and the distinct set shrinks to 1 value: ```sql SELECT DISTINCT intDiv(k, 25000) FROM (SELECT number AS k FROM numbers_mt(100000)) GROUP BY k LIMIT 3 SETTINGS max_threads = 16, max_block_size = 100; -- returns 1 row instead of 3 ``` **A window function in the projection** — is evaluated over all groups. `hasWindow()` only catches the named `WINDOW` clause, not inline `OVER ()`: ```sql SELECT count() OVER () AS w FROM (SELECT number AS k FROM numbers_mt(100000)) GROUP BY k LIMIT 5 SETTINGS max_threads = 16, max_block_size = 100; -- returns w = 100 instead of w = 100000 ``` **`arrayJoin` in the projection** — can drop rows (empty arrays), so `n + offset` kept groups may produce fewer rows than the LIMIT while more groups exist: ```sql SELECT arrayJoin(if(k % 1000 = 0, [k], [])) FROM (SELECT number AS k FROM numbers_mt(100000)) GROUP BY k LIMIT 10 SETTINGS max_threads = 16, max_block_size = 100; -- returns 1 row instead of 10 ``` **`QUALIFY`** — filters the groups after the aggregation, so the kept groups may not contain enough qualifying ones (a `QUALIFY` on plain group keys alone is pushed down below the aggregation and is not affected; a window function keeps it in place): ```sql SELECT count() OVER (PARTITION BY k % 2) AS w FROM (SELECT number AS k FROM numbers_mt(100000)) GROUP BY k QUALIFY k >= 99000 LIMIT 10 SETTINGS max_threads = 16, max_block_size = 100; -- returns 0 rows instead of 10 rows with w = 50000 ``` All four have the same root cause: the pass checks `HAVING`/`ORDER BY`/`WINDOW`/`LIMIT BY`/`GROUP BY` modifiers/aggregate functions, but not `DISTINCT`, `QUALIFY`, window function nodes or `arrayJoin` in the projection. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104473 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114690 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #114695 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1479` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Flaky test: 04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers reports zero preallocated sizes
signals.text: 🕵 `04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers` fails regularly on master and on many pull requests: the hash-table-sizes statistics come back as zero, so the test prints ``` final-prealloc 0 no-final-prealloc 0 ``` instead of the expected `520000` / `650000`. Per CIDB it failed 8 times on master in the last 30 days (most recently 2026-08-13 22:32:26), plus on 42 distinct pull requests, across every build flavour (`Fast test`, `arm_binary`, `amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `amd_llvm_coverage`), so it is not tied to a particular sanitizer, storage, or analyzer configuration. It also survives the automatic reruns ("Failed 3 out of 3 reruns"), which makes it look like a real regression in a job that hits it. Query for the history: ```sql SELECT toStartOfDay(check_start_time) AS day, count() AS failures, groupUniqArray(pull_request_number) AS prs FROM checks WHERE check_start_time >= now() - toIntervalDay(30) AND test_name = '04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers' AND test_status IN ('FAIL', 'ERROR') GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC ``` The test was last touched by 9650bb8cd624 (2026-07-23) "Fix flaky ... under randomized external aggregation", so the earlier flakiness fix looks incomplete. Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105987&sha=77de23431cd96d94d5370923e65911c42dc65480&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F3%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987

signals.title: Signed integer overflow reading Iceberg Decimal bounds with scale > 18
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong Reading an Iceberg table that contains a `Decimal` column with scale > 18 overflows `int64_t` while parsing the column bounds from the manifest. `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/ManifestFileIterator.cpp:95-99`: ```cpp if (int32_t scale = DB::getDecimalScale(*non_nullable_type)) { int64_t scaler = lower_bound ? -10 : 10; while (--scale) scaler *= 10; // overflows for scale > 18 unscaled_value += scaler; } ``` `Decimal(38, 30)` makes this compute 10^30 in an `int64_t`. Bounds are parsed for every column in the manifest entry, so any query with a filter is enough — the filter does not need to touch the Decimal column. On UBSan builds the process aborts. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce Tested against a `master` build, `26.8.1.1445`, `build_amd_asan_ubsan` from commit `236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949`: - CI run: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31840355042/job/94896049752 - Binary: https://clickhouse-builds.s3.amazonaws.com/REFs/master/236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949/build_amd_asan_ubsan/clickhouse [dec_min_iceberg_table.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31094087/dec_min_iceberg_table.tar.gz) Attached `dec_min_iceberg_table.tar.gz` is a two-column, one-row Iceberg table created by Spark: ```sql CREATE TABLE dec_min (id int, d decimal(38, 30)) USING iceberg TBLPROPERTIES ('format-version' = '2', 'write.format.default' = 'Parquet'); INSERT INTO dec_min SELECT 1, decimal(42.42); ``` ```bash curl -O https://clickhouse-builds.s3.amazonaws.com/REFs/master/236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949/build_amd_asan_ubsan/clickhouse chmod +x clickhouse CH=$PWD/clickhouse mkdir -p repro/user_files/lakehouses tar xzf dec_min_iceberg_table.tar.gz -C repro/user_files/lakehouses/ cd repro/user_files UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1 "$CH" local --path ../ \ --query "SELECT count() FROM icebergLocal('lakehouses/dec_min') WHERE id > 0" ``` ### Expected behavior No signed integer overflow. ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` /ClickHouse/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/ManifestFileIterator.cpp:97:28: runtime error: signed integer overflow: -1000000000000000000 * 10 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t' (aka 'long') #0 0x5e90f8391593 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x3de33593) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #1 0x5e90f838f2d8 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x3de312d8) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #2 0x5e90f8391fa7 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x3de33fa7) (BuildId: (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x3ddce395) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #5 0x5e90ea23b1b4 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x2fcdd1b4) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #6 0x5e90ea23d1e1 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x2fcdf1e1) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #7 0x5e90ea24f996 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x2fcf1996) (BuildId: 29ef547fc49ecdd123f1107ed1b548db382afaa7) #8 0x5e90d8ebc100 (/home/carlos/ClickHouse/ci/tmp/clickhouse+0x1e95e100) (BuildId: (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6+0x129d6b) (BuildId: 328820b908de8ea1ef79afa8995e302e819163d7) SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior /ClickHouse/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/ManifestFileIterator.cpp:97:28 Aborted ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Possibly caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78242 ### Additional context #### AI-assisted analysis The notes below were produced with AI assistance while triaging the failure. They are code reading, not measurements — treat them as a starting point, not as conclusions. **The overflowed value looks like it is discarded.** A few lines below, only `Decimal32` and `Decimal64` are handled; anything else returns `std::nullopt`. `Decimal32` and `Decimal64` cap precision at 9 and 18 (`DataTypeDecimalBase.h:165-166`) and scale cannot exceed precision, so `scale > 18` implies `Decimal128` / `Decimal256`, which take that `std::nullopt` path. If that reading is right, on non-sanitizer builds the wrapped value never becomes a bound, and the practical effect is limited to sanitizer builds aborting. **Possible fix** — bail out before the multiplication, which would keep the same observable behaviour: ```cpp if (int32_t scale = DB::getDecimalScale(*non_nullable_type)) { /// 10^19 no longer fits in int64_t. if (scale > 18) return std::nullopt; int64_t scaler = lower_bound ? -10 : 10; while (--scale) scaler *= 10; unscaled_value += scaler; } ``` Not compiled or tested. **Possibly a second issue on line 73**, `sign_extension <<= (str.size() * 8)`, which would shift by 128 for a 16-byte `Decimal128` bound. I could not trigger it — my test value was positive, so that branch was not taken.

signals.title: Paimon incremental read: a Keeper watermark left ahead of the warehouse (e.g. after restore) silently and permanently skips committed data
signals.text: ## Describe what's wrong A Paimon table read with incremental reads enabled (`paimon_incremental_read = 1`, which keeps a consumed-snapshot watermark in Keeper at `<paimon_keeper_path>/committed_snapshot`) can **silently and permanently skip durably-committed data** if the Keeper watermark is ever left ahead of the warehouse's latest snapshot id — for example after the Paimon warehouse is restored from an older backup, or is rolled back / truncated by another engine, while the ClickHouse Keeper cursor is not correspondingly reset. `PaimonMetadata::collectIncrementalDataFiles` resolves the resume point by comparing the Keeper watermark to the warehouse's current latest snapshot id, and treats "watermark `>=` latest" as an unconditional no-new-data case: ```cpp else if (*committed_snapshot_id >= state->snapshot_id) // PaimonMetadata.cpp:825 { LOG_DEBUG(log, "Snapshot {} already processed (committed={}), no new data", // :828 state->snapshot_id, *committed_snapshot_id); return {}; // :830 } ``` There is no read-repair and no error on this path — it returns an empty file list at `LOG_DEBUG`. So every snapshot the writer commits after the restore whose id is `<=` the stale watermark is never delivered to any consumer, with no exception and no user-visible log. Snapshots committed *above* the stale watermark resume normally, which makes the loss a silent hole rather than a total stall. The table-identity guard `validateTableIdentity` does not catch this: it re-reads schema-0 `timeMillis`, which is unchanged by a byte-copy restore, so the guard passes and the stale watermark is trusted. This is distinct from the *documented* At-Most-Once loss (`PaimonStreamState.h:35-37`), which concerns the window between advancing the watermark and finishing consumption *within a single poll*; here durably-committed data that no consumer ever received is dropped at resume time. This surface is behind the experimental setting `allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine` (default off). ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — reproduced on `26.8.1.1`; the code on current `master` is identical (`PaimonMetadata.cpp:825-830`). ## How to reproduce Requires the experimental Paimon engine and a Paimon warehouse (e.g. written with `pypaimon`), read via `PaimonLocal` with incremental reads and a Keeper cursor: 1. Create a warehouse with snapshots 1..3 (300 distinct rows) under the server's `user_files/`. Back up the warehouse directory at the snapshot-1 point. 2. `CREATE TABLE pt (...) ENGINE = PaimonLocal('<table_path>') SETTINGS paimon_incremental_read = 1, paimon_keeper_path = '/paimon/cursor', paimon_replica_name = 'r1'` with `allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine = 1`. 3. Poll `SELECT ... FROM pt` incrementally — all 300 rows are delivered and the Keeper watermark reaches 3. 4. Restore the warehouse directory from the snapshot-1 backup (schema unchanged). Have the Paimon writer append two new snapshots of new, distinct rows — these become snapshots 2 and 3 again (ids `<=` the stale watermark 3). 5. Poll again (and once more): **zero of the new rows are returned, no error is raised**, and the Keeper watermark stays 3. 6. Append one further snapshot (snapshot 4, id `>` 3): only snapshot 4's rows are returned — confirming the consumer is alive and the loss is confined to the snapshots at id `<=` the stale watermark. Controls that isolate the cause: reading the same restored-and-re-appended warehouse under a **fresh** `paimon_keeper_path` delivers all the new rows (so the warehouse content is intact and readable); and without the restore, appending snapshots above the watermark delivers normally. ## Expected behavior When the committed watermark is ahead of the warehouse's latest snapshot id (the warehouse has moved backwards relative to the cursor), ClickHouse should detect the disagreement and either fail loudly or reset the cursor to the warehouse state, rather than silently returning no data and permanently skipping every subsequent commit at id `<=` the stale watermark. ## Error message and/or stacktrace None — the defining property is that the skip is silent (only a `LOG_DEBUG` "no new data" line).

signals.title: Data loss with ATTACH PARTITION ... ON CLUSTER in ReplicatedMergeTree
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong We are running a 2-shard bare-metal cluster: - Shard 1: 2 replicas (ReplicatedMergeTree) - Shard 2: 1 replica (single node with no replication) We use a staging-to-target table pattern for our ETL, following the official [ClickLoad guidelines](https://clickhouse.com/blog/supercharge-your-clickhouse-data-loads-part3) which suggest using ON CLUSTER for sharded clusters: "The [MOVE PARTITION operations](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickLoad/blob/main/src/worker.py#L592) must run on all shards in a sharded cluster, e.g., by utilizing the [ON CLUSTER](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/sql-reference/distributed-ddl) clause" We found a critical issue where about half of our data disappears / goes missing if we run the ATTACH PARTITION command using ON CLUSTER. `ALTER TABLE target_local ATTACH PARTITION 202608 FROM staging_local ON CLUSTER 'my_cluster';` ### The Issue: - When we run this query with `ON CLUSTER`, it executes on all replicas concurrently. - The result is **massive data loss.** The target table ends up with only about half of the expected row count, and the rest of the data seems to vanish (some parts might end up stuck or lost during the concurrent move). ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce ClickHouse Version: 26.3.12.3 (or any recent stable version) Cluster topology: Sharded cluster with ReplicatedMergeTree (at least 2 replicas on one of the shards). Steps: 1. Load a large volume of data into a staging table (generating a high number of active data parts). 2. Execute the partition promotion using ON CLUSTER: `ALTER TABLE target_local ATTACH PARTITION 202608 FROM staging_local ON CLUSTER 'my_cluster';` 3. Under high part count and concurrency, this triggers write conflicts in ZooKeeper. ### Expected behavior The partition should attach successfully on all replicas without data loss. The ON CLUSTER coordination should safely execute the ATTACH on a single replica per shard and let standard replication handle the rest, rather than having all replicas concurrently attempt ZooKeeper registration. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context ### My Questions: 1. Why does running ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM ... ON CLUSTER cause data loss on ReplicatedMergeTree tables? Is this a known bug or a race condition with ZooKeeper? 2. Is there any way to safely use ON CLUSTER for this staging pattern without risking data deletion/loss? 3. Is external orchestration (e.g., triggering the DDL locally on exactly one replica per shard) the officially recommended way to handle this on bare-metal deployments?

signals.title: DeltaLake: trivial `SELECT count()` over a table with deletion vectors counts the deleted rows (`numRecords` summed, DV cardinality ignored)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** A Delta table where a `DELETE` was persisted as a deletion vector (the default for Spark/Databricks-written tables with `delta.enableDeletionVectors = true`) returns a wrong `SELECT count()`: the trivial-count path answers from file-level `numRecords` statistics and never subtracts the deletion vector's `cardinality`, so every DV-deleted row is still counted. Any query that actually scans the data (`sum`, `min`/`max`, a selective predicate) returns the correct result — the deletion-vector *scan* path works — which makes the wrong `count()` inconsistent with every other answer the same table gives. Version-pinned reads via `delta_lake_snapshot_version` have the same wrong count. `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` is a workaround. `optimize_count_from_files = 0` does **not** help — the shortcut is the storage's `totalRows`, not the files-count path. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1448 (also checked master snapshots back to 26.8.1.820). **How to reproduce** Write a table with a deletion vector using Spark (`pip install pyspark==3.5.3 delta-spark==3.2.1`, needs a JRE): ```python from delta import configure_spark_with_delta_pip from pyspark.sql import SparkSession b = (SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]") .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")) spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(b).getOrCreate() spark.sql("CREATE TABLE t (k BIGINT, v BIGINT) USING delta LOCATION '/tmp/dv_table' TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableDeletionVectors = true)") spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300)") spark.sql("DELETE FROM t WHERE k < 50") # persisted as a deletion vector, cardinality 50 spark.sql("INSERT INTO t SELECT id, id*10 FROM range(300, 310)") ``` The table now holds 260 rows (Spark: `SELECT count(*)` → 260, `VERSION AS OF 2` → 250). Then: ```bash clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table')" # 310 <- wrong, counts the 50 DV-deleted rows clickhouse local -q "SELECT count(), sum(k), min(k) FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table')" # 260 46670 50 <- scan path, correct clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0" # 260 <- workaround clickhouse local -q "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/dv_table') SETTINGS delta_lake_snapshot_version = 2" # 300 <- wrong; Spark's VERSION AS OF 2 says 250 (a scanning query with the same pin correctly returns 250) ``` An `strace` of the wrong read shows neither the data files nor the `deletion_vector_*.bin` file is ever opened — only the `_delta_log` JSON files. **Expected behavior** `SELECT count()` returns 260 (and 250 at `delta_lake_snapshot_version = 2`), matching what the same queries return when they scan. **Actual behavior** 310 and 300: the count is answered from metadata as the plain sum of `numRecords` across add actions, ignoring each file's `deletionVector.cardinality`. **Mechanism** `DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel::totalRows` serves the trivial-count from `TableSnapshot::getTotalRows`. Both row-accumulation sites in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/DeltaLake/TableSnapshot.cpp` (the scan callback that fills `data_files`, and the `StatsVisitor` stats-only path) receive the file's `dv_info` handle from delta-kernel, yet unconditionally do `total_rows.value() += stats->num_records`. Fail-close would be setting `total_rows = std::nullopt` whenever `dv_info` is present (forcing the scan path); the precise fix is subtracting the deletion vector's cardinality. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/93852 --- Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: Paimon incremental read: the unfenced processing_lock lets a second consumer silently duplicate acknowledged rows after a session expiry
signals.text: ## Describe what's wrong The Paimon incremental-read stream state (`allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine`) coordinates competing consumers that share one `paimon_keeper_path` with an ephemeral `processing_lock` znode. That lock has **no fencing**, so if the lock is lost while a consumer is mid-read (the usual cause being a Keeper session expiry that auto-removes the holder's ephemeral node), a second consumer acquires the freed lock and re-reads the same committed snapshot range. Both consumers then deliver the same committed data — an at-least-once **duplicate of already-acknowledged rows, with no error logged anywhere**. The `processing_lock` exists precisely to make the read/commit critical section mutually exclusive, so this defeats its only purpose. The unfenced-ness is visible in three places in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonStreamState.cpp` (line numbers on `master`): 1. Acquire writes the owner's `replica_name` into the lock node but it is **never read back** anywhere — the value is dead (`acquireProcessingLock`, lines 70–90): ```cpp keeper->create(processing_lock_path, replica_name, zkutil::CreateMode::Ephemeral); ``` 2. Release is an **unconditional** `tryRemove(path, -1)` whose return code is discarded, so it deletes whatever node is at the path — including an ephemeral created by a *different* session (`removeProcessingLock`, lines 269–274): ```cpp keeper->tryRemove(processing_lock_path, -1); ``` 3. The watermark advance is a **blind** `makeSetRequest(..., -1)` in its own standalone `tryMulti` with no check op on the lock and no monotonicity guard, so it succeeds regardless of whether the caller still holds the lock or whether another consumer moved the watermark underneath it (`setCommittedSnapshot`, lines 214–238): ```cpp ops.emplace_back(zkutil::makeSetRequest(committed_path, toString(snapshot_id), -1)); ``` For contrast, the sibling `is_active` node in the *same file* is fenced correctly — it reads the node back with its `Stat` and removes it version-checked (`tryGet(is_active_path, existing_identifier, &stat)` then `tryRemove(is_active_path, stat.version)`, lines ~159 and ~165) — so applying the same discipline to `processing_lock` is clearly feasible. Note this is distinct from the documented "at-most-once" window (a *loss* on crash between watermark advance and delivery): the issue here is a **duplicate with no crash**, produced by a routine session expiry, which an at-most-once contract does not permit. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes, reproduces on current `master`. The Paimon storage engine is experimental (`allow_experimental_paimon_storage_engine`, default off). ## How to reproduce Two ClickHouse instances (two Keeper sessions), each with a Paimon incremental-read table over the **same** warehouse and the **same** `paimon_keeper_path`: ```sql -- on both servers CREATE TABLE c (id Int64, v String) ENGINE = PaimonLocal('/warehouse/db.db/t1') SETTINGS paimon_incremental_read = 1, paimon_keeper_path = '/paimon/stream', paimon_replica_name = 'ra'; -- 'rb' on the second server ``` 1. Commit snapshot 1 to the warehouse; consumer A drains it, so `committed_snapshot` = 1. 2. Commit snapshots 2 and 3 (ids above the watermark). 3. Consumer A starts an incremental read: it acquires `processing_lock`, reads `committed_snapshot` (still 1), and plans the read of snapshots 2–3. 4. Consumer A's Keeper session expires (network blip / GC pause / Keeper failover exceeding `session_timeout_ms`). A's ephemeral `processing_lock` is auto-removed, but A's in-flight read continues (its server process is alive; the ZooKeeper client reconnects on a fresh session). 5. Consumer B polls: it acquires the now-free `processing_lock`, reads `committed_snapshot` (still 1, because A has not advanced it yet), and delivers snapshots 2–3. 6. Consumer A finishes: its blind `setCommittedSnapshot(3)` succeeds (version `-1`), and A also delivers snapshots 2–3. Both consumers have now delivered snapshots 2–3 — the same committed rows twice, with no error. The window in step 3–4 is deterministically reproducible by pausing A's `setCommittedSnapshot` multi to Keeper and deleting the `processing_lock` znode during the pause (which is exactly what a session expiry does to the ephemeral), then letting B poll and finally releasing A. ## Expected behavior Each committed snapshot is delivered to at most one consumer. A consumer that lost its `processing_lock` (session expiry, or the node otherwise gone) must not silently commit over another consumer's progress: the watermark advance and the lock release should be fenced by lock ownership (e.g. a version/session check, as `is_active` already does) so that a stale holder fails loudly instead of duplicating acknowledged data. ## Error message and/or stacktrace None — this is the problem. No exception is thrown and nothing is logged; the duplication is silent. ## Additional context The three call sites above are all in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonStreamState.cpp`.

signals.title: Azure data lake table engines (IcebergAzure, DeltaLakeAzure, PaimonAzure) do not mask credentials in SHOW CREATE TABLE and system.tables.engine_full
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** The Azure data lake table engines — `IcebergAzure`, `DeltaLakeAzure`, `PaimonAzure` — do not mask credentials in `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, `system.tables.engine_full`, or any other surface that formats the engine arguments with secrets hidden. Both the connection-string form (the `AccountKey=...` stays verbatim inside the string) and the 5-argument form (the `account_key` positional stays verbatim) leak, at the default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0` and without the `displaySecretsInShowAndSelect` privilege. Any user who can run `SHOW CREATE TABLE` or read `system.tables` sees the storage account key. The `AzureBlobStorage` engine with the very same argument shapes masks correctly (`AccountKey=[HIDDEN]` inside the connection string, `'[HIDDEN]'` for the positional), and so do all the Azure *table functions* (`azureBlobStorage`, `icebergAzure`, `deltaLakeAzure`, `paimonAzure` and their `*Cluster` variants) — a `CREATE VIEW ... AS SELECT * FROM icebergAzure(...)` masks fine. Only the three lake *engines* leak. **Affected versions** Reproduced on master `26.8.1.1448`; by code inspection the gap exists on every version that has the engines — the release tags `v26.4.2.10-stable` and `v25.3.1.2703-lts` both register `IcebergAzure` (26.4 also `DeltaLakeAzure`) while their `findTableEngineSecretArguments` dispatch lists neither, and `git log -S "IcebergAzure"` over the secret finder's history is empty, so the engines were never masked since their introduction (not a regression). **How to reproduce** The engine needs a reachable Azure endpoint to create the table, so the repro uses Azurite (`npm install azurite`) and creates the container named `test`. > Note: the `Eby8vdM02...` account key below is NOT a real credential — it is the well-known public account key of the `devstoreaccount1` emulator account, documented by Microsoft, shipped by every Azure storage emulator, and already used throughout this repository's own tests (e.g. `tests/queries/0_stateless/03582_azure_double_free.sh`). It is used here precisely so the repro works against Azurite out of the box. ```bash npx azurite-blob --blobHost 127.0.0.1 --blobPort 10000 --location /tmp/azurite --silent & python3 -c " from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient key = 'Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==' BlobServiceClient.from_connection_string('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=' + key + ';BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1;').create_container('test')" ``` ```sql CREATE TABLE ice_az ENGINE = IcebergAzure('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==;BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1;', 'test', 'ice') AS SELECT toInt64(number) AS k FROM numbers(10) SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1; SHOW CREATE TABLE ice_az; -- ENGINE = IcebergAzure('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==;BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1;', 'test', 'ice', 'Parquet') -- ^^^ raw account key SELECT engine_full FROM system.tables WHERE name = 'ice_az'; -- same raw connection string CREATE TABLE az (k Int64) ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==;BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1;', 'test', 'plain.parquet', 'Parquet'); SHOW CREATE TABLE az; -- ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=[HIDDEN];BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1;', 'test', 'plain.parquet', 'Parquet') -- ^^^ masked, same DDL shape ``` The 5-argument form leaks the same way: `IcebergAzure('http://.../devstoreaccount1', 'test', 'ice', 'devstoreaccount1', '<account_key>')` keeps the raw key in `SHOW CREATE`, while `AzureBlobStorage` with the same positionals shows `'[HIDDEN]'`. **Mechanism** The table-engine dispatch in `FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder::findTableEngineSecretArguments` (`src/Parsers/FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder.cpp`) lists the S3-family lake engines (`DeltaLake`, `DeltaLakeS3`, `Hudi`, `Iceberg`, `IcebergS3`, `Paimon`, `PaimonS3`, `S3Queue`) in the S3 branch and `AzureBlobStorage` / `AzureQueue` in the Azure branch, but `IcebergAzure`, `DeltaLakeAzure` and `PaimonAzure` appear in neither, so none of their arguments are ever marked secret. The *table function* dispatch in the same file does cover `icebergAzure` / `deltaLakeAzure` / `paimonAzure` (routing to `findAzureBlobStorageFunctionSecretArguments`), which is why views over the table functions mask while the engines leak. `IcebergAzure` (`DeltaLakeAzure`, `PaimonAzure`) presumably just need to join `AzureBlobStorage` / `AzureQueue` in the engine branch (they take the same leading argument shape). Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: SAS token in the URL argument of AzureBlobStorage / azureBlobStorage is not masked in SHOW CREATE, engine_full and query_log
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** An Azure SAS token embedded in the URL argument of the `AzureBlobStorage` engine / `azureBlobStorage` table function is not masked: the full token, including the `sig=` signature, appears verbatim in `SHOW CREATE TABLE`, `system.tables.engine_full`, and `system.query_log.query` at default `format_display_secrets_in_show_and_select = 0`. The URL-with-SAS spelling is a documented, working authentication form: when the URL contains `?`, everything after it is used as `sas_auth` (`src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/ObjectStorages/AzureBlobStorage/AzureBlobStorageCommon.cpp`, `processURL`), and the integration test `test_storage_azure_blob_storage/test.py::test_sas_token` exercises exactly this form. A SAS token is a bearer credential — anyone holding it gets the granted container access until expiry. The equivalent connection-string spelling (`...;SharedAccessSignature=...`) IS masked (as `[HIDDEN]`), and the positional `account_key` argument IS masked, so the URL spelling is the one gap: `FunctionSecretArgumentsFinder` masks designated secret argument positions, and a URL argument is treated as non-secret even when it carries the credential. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1448 (official build). 20/20 deterministic. **How to reproduce** No Azure endpoint is needed — with SAS auth the engine skips the container existence probe, so the CREATE succeeds against an unreachable address: ```sql CREATE TABLE sas_leak (k Int64) ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('http://127.0.0.1:1/devstoreaccount1/cont/?sv=2025-01-05&sp=rl&sr=c&sig=SYNTHETICSIGNATUREVALUE', '', 'data.parquet', 'Parquet'); SHOW CREATE TABLE sas_leak; -- ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('http://127.0.0.1:1/devstoreaccount1/cont/?sv=2025-01-05&sp=rl&sr=c&sig=SYNTHETICSIGNATUREVALUE', '', 'data.parquet', 'Parquet') -- the token is verbatim; expected [HIDDEN] for the SAS query string SELECT engine_full FROM system.tables WHERE name = 'sas_leak'; -- same verbatim token -- the table function leaks through the query log even when the query itself fails: SELECT count() FROM azureBlobStorage('http://127.0.0.1:1/devstoreaccount1/cont/?sv=2025-01-05&sp=rl&sr=c&sig=SYNTHETICSIGNATUREVALUE', '', 'data.parquet', 'Parquet'); -- fails, endpoint unreachable SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS query_log; SELECT count() FROM system.query_log WHERE query LIKE '%SYNTHETICSIGNATUREVALUE%' AND query LIKE '%azureBlobStorage%'; -- >= 1 ``` Contrast (masked correctly): ```sql CREATE TABLE conn_ok (k Int64) ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=a;BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:1/a;SharedAccessSignature=sv=2025-01-05&sig=SYNTHETICSIGNATUREVALUE', 'cont', 'data.parquet', 'Parquet'); SHOW CREATE TABLE conn_ok; -- ENGINE = AzureBlobStorage('[HIDDEN]', 'cont', 'data.parquet', 'Parquet') ``` **Expected behavior** The SAS query string in a URL argument is masked the same way the connection-string `SharedAccessSignature=` spelling and `account_key` are — at minimum the `sig=` parameter value. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75045 Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: Is ATTACH PARTITION FROM ... ON CLUSTER safe on replicated tables, or should we execute on a single replica?
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Question We are designing a staging-to-target partition promotion flow on our on-premise, bare-metal cluster using ReplicatedMergeTree with ClickHouse Keeper. We are confused by two conflicting recommendations regarding DDL distribution: 1. **The Official ClickHouse Blog** ([ClickLoad Series](https://clickhouse.com/blog/supercharge-your-clickhouse-data-loads-part3)): It recommends using `ON CLUSTER` for sharded clusters: > > "The MOVE PARTITION operations must run on all shards in a sharded cluster, e.g., by utilizing the ON CLUSTER clause." > > However, on a replicated cluster, `ON CLUSTER` distributes the `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` DDL to **every single replica** of every shard, executing them concurrently. 2. **The Community Guide** ([OneUptime Detach/Attach in Replication](https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-clickhouse-replication-detach-attach-partitions/view)): It explicitly notes that `ATTACH PARTITION` and `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` are automatically replicated: > > "You only need to run the command on one replica - the other replicas will perform the same operation automatically." > > ### My Questions: - If `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` is automatically replicated under `ReplicatedMergeTree`, doesn't using `ON CLUSTER` (as recommended in ClickLoad) cause race conditions or duplicate execution issues among replicas of the same shard? - Does this mean we should avoid `ON CLUSTER` and instead build a custom orchestrator to target and execute the query on exactly one replica per shard? - Is there any plan to make `ATTACH/MOVE PARTITION ... ON CLUSTER` replication-aware so it automatically delegates to a single replica per shard?

signals.title: Segmentation guard gated on `balance > 0` drops the old unconditional size cap
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **Feeding non-JSON bytes containing no opening bracket to `JSONEachRow` with `input_format_parallel_parsing=1` buffers the entire input into a single segmentation `Memory<>` before failing. The old code threw as soon as the segment exceeded `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — the `balance > 0` conjunct. The check it replaced (`min_bytes != 0 && current_object_size > 10 * min_bytes`) was unconditional, so it also bounded bytes accumulated outside any object. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ParallelParsingInputFormat` segmentator -> `JSONUtils::fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRow` -> `fileSegmentationEngineJSONEachRowImpl` ([`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53)). The size check is now inside `if (max_row_size && balance > 0)`. While no opening bracket has been seen `balance` stays 0, `find_first_symbols` scans to the buffer end, `continue` re-enters `loadAtPosition`, and the segment grows with no bound until EOF. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L53) — size check gated on balance > 0 - [`src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp:111`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/Formats/JSONUtils.cpp#L111) — object_start_bytes updated only when balance reaches 0 **Impact:** The DoS protection that `01701_parallel_parsing_infinite_segmentation.sh` was written to guard is weakened: malformed input that never opens a bracket (truncated files, an HTML error page piped into `JSONEachRow`, JSONEachRow data sent to `JSONCompactEachRow` where the searched bracket is `[`) is buffered in full instead of being rejected at `10 * min_chunk_bytes_for_parallel_parsing` (100 MiB with defaults). Transient memory per malformed request grows from a bounded 100 MiB to the full input size. Because `input_format_json_max_object_size` is also not consulted anywhere on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow` data path, the segmentation engine is the only enforcement point for this format. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `da67f74224255`). ### How to reproduce _See root cause description and affected locations above._ ### Expected behavior ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Size of JSON object at position ... is extremely large. Expected not greater than 1048576 bytes, but current is ... bytes per object. Increase the value of setting 'input_format_json_max_object_size' or check your data manually, most likely JSON is malformed. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Unexpected eof: (at row 0) : (in file/uri (fd = 0)): While executing JSONEachRowRowInputFormat: While executing File. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Drop the `balance > 0` conjunct and keep `object_start_bytes` as the anchor: `if (max_row_size)` still measures bytes since the last completed object, which is the intended semantics and additionally bounds inter-object garbage. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `input_format_json_max_object_size` is never read on the non-parallel `JSONEachRow`/`JSONCompactEachRow` data-parsing path with a known schema (verified: with `--input_format_json_max_object_size=1000 --structure='a String'`, a 50007-byte object is accepted at `input_format_parallel_parsing=0` and rejected at `=1`), which contradicts the setting description in `src/Core/FormatFactorySettings.h` ("The same limit is applied in both parallel and non-parallel parsing paths"). Found during automated review of [PR #107669](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107669). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr107669_002` </details> cc @Avogar @Manerone (from #107669)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: New 1 GiB JSON guard measures the whole column chars buffer, not one value
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **Valid JSON input is rejected with `Code: 131. DB::Exception: JSON string is too large, maximum size is 1073741824 bytes` even though no individual string comes close to 1 GiB. Whether the same file is accepted or rejected depends on `max_block_size`.** - **Root cause:** [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) uses `s.size()` as a proxy for the current value's length. `s` is an append-target that callers pre-populate; the correct quantity is `s.size()` minus the size recorded at function entry. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `JSONEachRowRowInputFormat::readRow` -> `SerializationString::deserializeTextJSON` ([`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:536`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L536)) passes `ColumnString::Chars & data` — the destination column's whole chars buffer, which already holds every previous row of the current block — as the `Vector & s` argument of `readJSONStringInto`. The new check at [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) tests `s.size()`, i.e. the accumulated column size, not the size of the value being read. **Affected locations:** - [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1298`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1298) — readJSONStringInto: check on cumulative destination vector size - [`src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp:1356`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/IO/ReadHelpers.cpp#L1356) — readJSONObjectOrArrayPossiblyInvalid: identical cumulative check - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:536`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L536) — passes ColumnString::Chars (whole block) as the append target - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp:502`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationString.cpp#L502) — same for readJSONObjectPossiblyInvalid under input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings - [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationFixedString.cpp:292`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/da67f74224255/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationFixedString.cpp#L292) — passes ColumnFixedString::Chars as the append target **Impact:** Any `JSONEachRow` ingest whose String/FixedString column accumulates more than 1 GiB within a single block now fails with `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` on perfectly valid data. `input_format_max_block_size_bytes` defaults to 0, so blocks are row-bounded only (`max_insert_block_size` ~ 1048449 rows for INSERT), i.e. ~1 KB average string length is enough. The limit is hardcoded and cannot be raised or disabled by any setting. The same check also fires inside the `ReturnType = bool` instantiations (`tryReadJSONStringInto`, `readJSONObjectPossiblyInvalid<..., bool>`), throwing where the try-contract requires returning `false`, so `Variant`/`Dynamic` fallbacks turn into query errors. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `da67f74224255`). ### How to reproduce _See root cause description and affected locations above._ ### Expected behavior ``` 3 1258291200 in both arms - no individual JSON string exceeds 1 GiB, so neither arm should be rejected, and the outcome must not depend on max_block_size. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Arm A (default max_block_size): Code: 131. DB::Exception: JSON string is too large, maximum size is 1073741824 bytes: (while reading the value of key a): (at row 3) : (in file/uri (fd = 0)): While executing JSONEachRowRowInputFormat: While executing File. (TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE) Arm B (max_block_size=2, identical data): 3 1258291200 Object variant (input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings=1), d ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Record `const size_t initial_size = s.size();` at function entry and compare `s.size() - initial_size` against the limit in both `readJSONStringInto` and `readJSONObjectOrArrayPossiblyInvalid`. Also route the `ReturnType = bool` instantiations through the existing `error()` lambda instead of an unconditional `throw`, and consider making the cap configurable rather than hardcoded. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `NullOutput::size()` was added returning 0, so the skip path is exempt — intentional, but it means the same input is bounded or unbounded depending on whether the column is materialized. Found during automated review of [PR #107669](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107669). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr107669_001` </details> cc @Avogar @Manerone (from #107669)

signals.title: Race condition on `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::(get/set)Paths`
signals.text: ClickHouse S3 related functions, when not using hive partitioning, supports writing multiple files to the same file path by appending a numbered counter at the end when using `s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1`. ``` create table s3_table (id UInt32) engine=s3(s3_conn, filename='root/file.parquet'); insert into s3_table values 1 SETTINGS s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1; insert into s3_table values 2 SETTINGS s3_create_new_file_on_insert=1; select _file, id from s3_table; "root/file.parquet", 1 "root/file.parquet.1", 2 ``` The way this has been implemented is through an in-memory vector keeping the paths produced by this function/ table so that the next insert knows the next filename and upon reading it is possible to enumerate all files. When the server re-starts, this information is lost and ClickHouse relies on a slow retry-mechanism to get the latest inserted file path. When looking at https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87592, I realized the `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::getPaths/setPaths` methods are not thread safe. AFAIK, `StorageObjectStorage::write` can be executed in parallel and does not impose any locking mechanism - which might result in the `paths` object being modified simultaneously. The obivous answer is to add protection around `(get/set)Paths`, but honestly wouldn't it be better if we just deprecated it since [hive partitioning is becoming the default](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86746)? The downside tho is that we would no longer support multiple writes to a fixed location without a partition strategy. Actually, it could also break the wildcard partition strategy in case the user is also relying on `s3_create_new_file_on_insert`

signals.title: `DataLakeCatalog()` with Polaris REST catalog duplicates S3 path prefix causing 404 errors
signals.text: ### Company or project name developer testing ClickHouse integration with Apache Polaris REST catalog. I can try to fix this in the next few days 🙏 ### Describe what's wrong When using `DataLakeCatalog()` engine to connect to Apache Polaris REST catalog with vended S3 credentials, ClickHouse incorrectly constructs the S3 object path by duplicating the table location path. This results in 404 errors when attempting to query tables. **Error pattern:** - Expected path: `bucket123/music/albums/metadata/00005-a4c1e01b-61ce-4131-9ea8-62591e3a9907.metadata.json` - Actual path: `music/albums/bucket123/music/albums/metadata/00005-a4c1e01b-61ce-4131-9ea8-62591e3a9907.metadata.json` The table location (`music/albums`) appears **twice** in the path, causing S3 to return 404. **Root cause:** The bug is in `src/Databases/DataLake/ICatalog.cpp` in the `constructLocation()` method https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4a90b95163ce2d626880356230bf04bef14b62c1/src/Databases/DataLake/ICatalog.cpp#L112-L132. When Polaris vends credentials with an S3 endpoint, the code constructs the full path by concatenating: 1. The vended endpoint from Polaris 2. The bucket name 3. The table path However, the table path already includes the full location, resulting in duplication. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce **Prerequisites:** 1. Apache Polaris 1.2.0-incubating running at `http://polaris:8181` 2. MinIO S3-compatible storage at `http://minio:9000` 3. Iceberg table created in Polaris catalog with location `s3://bucket123/music/albums` **Setup Polaris and MinIO using docker-compose:** ```yaml services: polaris: image: apache/polaris:1.2.0-incubating ports: - "8183:8181" environment: AWS_REGION: us-west-2 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: minio_root AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: m1n1opwd POLARIS_BOOTSTRAP_CREDENTIALS: POLARIS,root,s3cr3t minio: image: quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z ports: - "9000:9000" environment: MINIO_ROOT_USER: minio_root MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: m1n1opwd command: server /data ``` Clickhouse command ```sql SET allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1; DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS polaris_catalog; CREATE DATABASE polaris_catalog ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('http://polaris:8181/api/catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'rest', catalog_credential = 'root:s3cr3t', warehouse = 'quickstart_catalog', auth_scope = 'PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL', oauth_server_uri = 'http://polaris:8181/api/catalog/v1/oauth/tokens', auth_header = 'X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation:vended-credentials', storage_endpoint = 'http://minio:9000/bucket123'; USE polaris_catalog; -- This works (tables are discovered) SHOW TABLES; -- This fails with 404 error (path duplication) SELECT * FROM `music.albums`; ``` ### Expected behavior The query `SELECT * FROM 'music.albums'` should successfully read data from the Iceberg table by constructing the correct S3 path: [bucket123/music/albums/metadata/00005-*.metadata.json](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) ### Error message and/or stacktrace The log from the command above ``` SET allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1 Query id: 7a5eeee1-fad2-4392-ab4f-b3c140fb6a76 Ok. 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.014 sec. DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS polaris_catalog Query id: 158c32e7-60c7-4270-8eb9-7a72350ed239 Ok. 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.003 sec. CREATE DATABASE polaris_catalog ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('http://polaris:8181/api/catalog') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'rest', catalog_credential = 'root:s3cr3t', warehouse = 'quickstart_catalog', auth_scope = 'PRINCIPAL_ROLE:ALL', oauth_server_uri = 'http://polaris:8181/api/catalog/v1/oauth/tokens', auth_header = 'X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation:vended-credentials', storage_endpoint = 'http://minio:9000/bucket123' Query id: 56e6642a-cdda-416d-ac05-3cdb8c2d3e86 Ok. 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.007 sec. USE polaris_catalog Query id: d7c5da63-03ba-4197-8793-45e298995ef7 Ok. 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.001 sec. SHOW TABLES Query id: 8fa8856b-8a33-4531-9794-15815ffdc100 ┌─name─────────┐ 1. │ music.albums │ └──────────────┘ 1 row in set. Elapsed: 0.272 sec. SELECT * FROM `music.albums` Query id: 2f79611e-2582-409d-ba44-ce964d17851e Elapsed: 0.016 sec. Received exception from server (version 25.12.1): Code: 499. signals.title: ClickHouse roadmap 2026
signals.text: This is the ClickHouse roadmap 2026. This roadmap does not cover the tasks related to infrastructure, orchestration, documentation, marketing, external integrations, drivers, etc. See also: Roadmap 2025: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/74046 Roadmap 2024: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/58392 Roadmap 2023: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/44767 Roadmap 2022: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/32513 Roadmap 2021: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/17623 Roadmap 2020: [link](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/be29057de1835f6f4a17e03a422b45b81efe6833/docs/ru/whats-new/extended-roadmap.md) Roadmap 2019: [link](https://presentations.clickhouse.com/2018-roadmap/) Roadmap 2018: [link](https://presentations.clickhouse.com/2017-meetup11/news_and_plans/) ## Query Engine - [ ] Parallel replicas for Merge tables #67770 - [x] Materialized CTE #94849 - [ ] Optimization by combining aggregation with topK - [x] Optimization of aggregation with flat combining #79428 - [ ] Cache for deserialized columns - [ ] Cascades cost-based optimizer for JOINs - [ ] Using partition key to optimize JOINs - [ ] Using partition key to optimize DISTINCT, IN, GROUP BY, and LIMIT BY - [x] Runtime filters for JOINs by default - [ ] Optimization of anti-joins: LEFT JOIN ... WHERE ... IS NULL to NOT IN - [ ] Deriving index condition from the right-hand side of INNER JOIN - [x] Support for certain SQL functions without parentheses #52102 - [ ] Optimizations for a single dictionary in LowCardinality #72717 - [ ] Block-level hints (= algebraic properties of intermediate chunks: sortedness, uniqueness, clustering of identical values) #48800 - [x] Query cache for subqueries #51656 - [ ] Query cache for partial results #57490 - [ ] On-disk query cache #52141 - [x] Improvements for the query condition cache - [ ] Streaming queries #63312 - [x] Enable JIT compilation on macOS #100947 - [ ] Query plan caching #93812 ## Resiliency - [ ] Automatic external memory for DISTINCT and LIMIT BY - [ ] Automatic external memory for IN - [x] Automatic external memory for JOIN https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97813 - [x] Memory configuration in the workload scheduler #82414 - [ ] GROUP BY in order by default - [x] Automatic selection of max_insert_threads - [x] Tracking the space in external memory - [ ] Spill to S3 in addition to spill to the cache - [x] Allow the cancellation of scalar subqueries #100230 ## Data Storage - [x] Text index in GA - [ ] Unique key constraint #70589 - [ ] Automatic LowCardinality columns #69916 - [x] Compact statistics storage - [x] Statistics by default https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101275 - [ ] Virtual shards on top of shared storage ☁ - [x] Automatic buckets in Map data type [#99200](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99200) - [ ] Transactions for Replicated tables - [ ] Scoring in the text index ## Data Lakes - [x] Metadata caching for Parquet files - [ ] Support arbitrary nesting in database and table names #71171 - [ ] Support for case-insensitive database, table, and column names #33935 - [ ] Support for deletion vectors in Iceberg v3 - [x] Query Condition Cache for data lakes - [x] Lazy columns reading for data lakes - [ ] Data Lake catalogs in GA - [x] Automatic cluster functions for subqueries - [ ] Support for AWS S3 Tables - [x] Support for Google BigLake - [x] Plain Rewritable metadata storage to support hard links - [ ] Materialized views on top of data lakes - [ ] Background merges for data lakes ☁ ## Interfaces - [ ] Allow interactive queries to finish in the background #49683 - [ ] Configurable query rewrite rules #80084 - [ ] PromQL dialect in GA - [x] Support for Arrow Flight SQL - [ ] Kafka2 in GA - [x] Configuration of query handlers with SQL - [ ] Remote and Cloud database engines #59304 - [x] Drivers for UDFs #71172 - [x] WebAssembly UDFs - [ ] API for query construction #64336 - [ ] Even simpler data upload #38775 - [ ] Passing input data to the url table function #45994 - [x] Framing formats for query results - [ ] Predictive autocomplete in the CLI #69641 ## Cleanups - [ ] Remove old analyzer - [ ] Remove old predicate pushdown mechanics - [x] Remove the hypotheses index - [x] Remove Parquet reader v1 - [ ] Remove or fix Kusto (KQL) - [ ] Remove Window View in favor of streaming queries

signals.title: [CI crash] Segfault in ContextData destructor during MetricLog flush
signals.text: ### Overview Segfault at address `0x50` (null pointer with offset) during `MetricLog` flush in the `SystemLog` saving thread. The crash occurs during `ContextData::~ContextData` when destroying Context objects held by `InsertDependenciesBuilder`. **CI report**: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=98677&sha=ad456bbcb213b8e58952cf24390b4c6fe282fefb&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 ### Stack trace ``` sdallocx_default operator delete(void*, unsigned long) DB::ContextData::~ContextData() std::__shared_ptr_pointer<DB::Context*, ...>::__on_zero_shared() std::__hash_table<..., std::shared_ptr<DB::Context const>, ...>::__deallocate_node() DB::InsertDependenciesBuilder::~InsertDependenciesBuilder() DB::QueryPlanResourceHolder::~QueryPlanResourceHolder() DB::QueryPipeline::reset() DB::BlockIO::reset() DB::BlockIO::~BlockIO() DB::SystemLog<DB::MetricLogElement>::flushImpl() DB::SystemLog<DB::MetricLogElement>::savingThreadFunction() ``` ### Analysis - The crash is at address `0x50`, which is a null-like address — a `ContextData` member's internal pointer was corrupted before destruction. - The MetricLog flush thread is likely a victim of heap corruption originating from another source. The code path itself (`SystemLog::flushImpl` → `InterpreterInsertQuery` → `InsertDependenciesBuilder` context lifecycle) appears correct on inspection. - This occurred in the Stress test (arm_release) job, which is a release build without sanitizers. An ASan or TSan reproduction would be needed to identify the actual corruption source. - PR #98677 is CI-only (adds ARM stress tests), so this is a pre-existing bug exposed by new test coverage. - The crash happened ~1.5 hours into the stress test during normal operation (not during shutdown). Only one crash event, no prior fatal errors. - Version: 26.3.1.776, git hash: `92a2b37d5ab51b4d5d0042ea9876727e112727ec`, architecture: aarch64.

signals.title: Add `user_files_policy` server setting for custom disks in user_files directory
signals.text: Add a new `user_files_policy` server configuration parameter, similar to `tmp_policy`, that allows user files to reside on custom storage volumes, including S3-backed disks. When configured, the policy's volume (which must have exactly one volume) provides the disks for user file storage. All file operations (`file()` table function, `StorageFile`, dictionaries, `DatabaseFilesystem`, etc.) now route through the `IDisk` interface when a volume is configured, enabling S3 and other remote storage backends. Key changes: - `user_files_policy` setting in `ServerSettings` with XML config example - `Context` stores `VolumePtr` and exposes `getUserFilesVolume`, `getUserFilesPaths`, `setUserFilesPolicy` - `StorageFile` supports disk-based glob matching via `listFilesWithRegexpMatchingOnDisk`, disk-based reads via `disk->readFile`, and disk-based writes via `disk->writeFile` - `FunctionFile` reads through disk I/O when volume is configured - All 13 callers of `getUserFilesPath` updated for multi-path validation - Helper overloads `pathStartsWith(path, vector)` and `fileOrSymlinkPathStartsWith(path, vector)` added - Integration test with local multi-disk and S3 (`s3_plain`) scenarios ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `user_files_policy` server setting to store `user_files` on a custom disk, including S3-backed disks. This allows customers to have a "scratch area" for files in ClickHouse Cloud, shared among all replicas. Note: keeping as a draft, because the code is not generalized enough. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Introduces a new storage-policy-backed path for `user_files` and rewires many read/write and path-validation code paths (including remote disks), which could affect file access semantics and security boundaries if edge cases are missed. > > **Overview** > Adds a new server setting `user_files_policy` that binds the `user_files` directory to a storage policy (enforced to *exactly one volume with one disk*) and stores the resolved `VolumePtr` in `Context`, with server startup applying it via `setUserFilesPolicy`. > > Updates user-files consumers to become disk-aware when a policy is configured: `file()`/`StorageFile` switch to `IDisk`-based globbing, reads, writes, schema inference and truncation (plus new helpers like `splitUserFilesAbsolutePath`, `userFilesPathExists`, and symlink-escape checks), while features that require local POSIX paths (`ATTACH ... FROM`, SQLite, `filesystem` table function, static HTTP `file://`, FileLog, several dictionary sources, error logger, etc.) now explicitly reject remote `user_files_policy` disks. > > Adds integration coverage for local-disk and `s3_plain` configurations, including globbing, absolute paths, traversal/symlink-escape hardening, write/append/truncate behavior, schema inference, and expected rejections (e.g. partitioned inserts under `user_files_policy`). > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 04b03ad8df769f756aa699f0eb7eb7fff624da1b. signals.title: Add assertions in IColumn::mutate to verify deep unique ownership of sub-columns
signals.text: Investigation for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/99920 This is a draft PR with diagnostic assertions to help find a COW violation bug where columns stored in `HashJoin` have their `allocatedBytes()` change because internal sub-columns are modified by someone who treats immutable columns as mutable. ## What was found The bug manifests as `data->allocated_size != debug_allocated_size` exception in debug builds. Investigation narrowed it down to: 1. **Removing the single-chunk optimization** in `Squashing.cpp:70-72` fixes the bug — this optimization passes chunks through without `IColumn::mutate`, so columns remain shared with Memory engine blocks 2. The **modification happens between** `addBlockToJoin` calls — during pipeline processing of the next chunk 3. The mutation is a **reallocation** (reserve/grow), not a data write — `protect()` (mprotect) doesn't catch it 4. The assertions in this PR (`IColumn::mutate` deep ownership check) **do NOT fire** — meaning the mutation happens outside the `IColumn::mutate` path entirely. Someone treats an immutable column as mutable without going through `mutate`. ## Reproducer The test `04049_fix_hashjoin_shared_column_allocated_size` reproduces the exception in debug builds. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Fix vertical merge nested default corruption
signals.text: ### Summary --- Vertical merge gathers columns one at a time. When a column has `DEFAULT` that references another column which is absent from all source parts and has no `DEFAULT` itself – that dependency is already expired and won't be in the block during evaluateMissingDefaults. Expression engine substitutes a typeless empty value for it, the resulting column gets wrong outer array dimensions, and this corrupts shared Nested offsets when written to the merged part. This is challenge (1) from [#91127](https://github.com/germiBest/ClickHouse/issues/91127). Fix extends existing column expiration logic to transitively expire columns whose DEFAULT depends on already-expired column. Since these columns were never present in any source part, read path was already computing them on-the-fly with full column context available – so expiring them during merge changes nothing for the end user. Fixes [#86123](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/86123). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix silent data corruption during vertical merge when a Nested subcolumn added via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN has a DEFAULT expression that depends on another missing column without a default. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Add `borrow_from_cache` object storage and `memory` metadata types
signals.text: Add a new object storage type `borrow_from_cache` that allocates space in a named filesystem cache using ephemeral `FileSegment`s. Each stored object is backed by a cache segment held alive via `FileSegmentsHolder`; when released, the cache reclaims the space. Add a new metadata type `memory` that keeps all file-to-blob mappings and directory structure entirely in memory with no persistence. On server restart all data is lost, which is acceptable for the intended use case of temporary tables. Configuration example: ``` disk(type=object_storage, object_storage_type='borrow_from_cache', metadata_type='memory', cache_name='some_cache') ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A new object storage type and metadata type suitable for temporary tables. Add a new object storage type `borrow_from_cache` that allocates space in a named filesystem cache and holds it from eviction. Add a new metadata storage type `memory` that keeps the mapping in memory. For example, this could allow creating temporary tables with custom engines in the Cloud without using S3. Closes #75551.
