signals.title: SQLancer: track sqlancer main, deduplicate findings, fail the job on them
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes Not user-facing. ### Description Three fixes to the nightly SQLancer job (`NightlySQLancer`, every 3 days). #### 1. Fuzz `ClickHouse/sqlancer` `main`, not a hardcoded commit The image pinned `ClickHouse/sqlancer@a62ea509`, so oracle work landing in the fork never reached CI. Pointing the Dockerfile at a branch is not enough: praktika rebuilds an image only when its directory digest changes, so a branch fetched at image-build time freezes at whatever `main` was when the Dockerfile was last edited — worse than an explicit pin, because it silently lies about what is being fuzzed. Instead: - the image clones `main` as a **warm cache** and keeps `.git` plus the maven repository under `/sqlancer` (world-writable, so the job's non-root user can extend it); - `sqlancer_job.sh` **re-clones and rebuilds `main` at job start** (~1 min with the warm maven repo) and falls back to the baked build if GitHub or Maven is unavailable; - the resolved commit is printed and included in the job info, so a finding stays attributable after `main` moves. Overrides for a one-off run: `SQLANCER_REF`, `SQLANCER_REPO`, `SQLANCER_BUILD_AT_RUNTIME=0`. #### 2. Readable output: one artifact per finding, deduplicated Before, the job log was ~3600 progress lines for a 5h run plus, for every finding, the whole reproducer state dump that SQLancer's `AlsoWriteToConsoleFileWriter` mirrors to stderr — impossible to read, and the reproducers were only available as one tarball of everything. Now the console shows one progress line per ~5 minutes and a summary (~20 lines for a clean run); the full fuzzer output remains an artifact. Findings are reported individually **and** deduplicated: - Each `logs/clickhouse/databaseN.log` is exactly one finding (`StateLogger.logException` writes the stack trace plus that database's whole `CREATE`/`INSERT`/…/`SELECT` sequence, then the worker continues under a fresh database name), so each is copied out and attached as its own artifact. - New `ci/jobs/scripts/sqlancer_failures.py` fingerprints every finding as **(exception class + ClickHouse error code/name from the `Caused by:` chain, reporting oracle, first sqlancer stack frame)** and groups equal fingerprints. - The report gets one row per *distinct* failure with the individual findings and their logs nested underneath, plus `failures/analysis.txt` (all families, loudest first, and a per-finding index). The failure *message* is deliberately **not** part of the fingerprint: for most oracles it is the generated SQL, unique to every finding, which would defeat the dedup. To keep that safe, every family lists all of its occurrences by database name and up to three distinct *message shapes* (literals → `'S'`, numbers → `N`, generated identifiers such as `c0`/`t3`/`database7` → `id`), so a family that merged more than one bug is visible as such. The job info line becomes, for example: ``` sqlancer main @ 3a66cc5ce597; 1,407k queries; 43 finding(s) in 13 distinct failure(s): PivotedQuerySynthesisBase/Code 241 x20, NoREC/Code 241 x8, TLPDistinct/AssertionError x3, ... ``` and the rows: ``` Failure analysis [analysis.txt] PivotedQuerySynthesisBase / AssertionError / Code 241 (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) / at SQLQueryAdapter.checkException:176 (x20) |- database0 [database0.log] \- ... TLPDistinct / AssertionError / at ComparatorHelper.assumeResultSetsAreEqual:127 (x3) |- database48 [database48.log] \- ... ``` If the analysis script itself fails, the job still fails and attaches the raw reproducer logs, so a bug in it can never swallow a finding. #### 3. A finding now marks the job failed Praktika derives the GitHub job conclusion from the job script's **exit code** (`res = run_code == 0` in `ci/praktika/runner.py`); the result file's status only drives the HTML report. Both SQLancer scripts exited 0 unconditionally, so a finding could not turn the nightly red. They now exit non-zero whenever anything was found: - a reproducer log; - a sanitizer report or `<Fatal>` message in the server logs (this job runs an ASan+UBSan build) — checked before the server is stopped, so a leak report emitted during shutdown does not turn every run red; - a dead or unreachable server; - a non-zero sqlancer exit code; - a run that produced no execution statistics at all (silently broken run). `sqlancer_pp_job.sh` additionally wrote the invalid status tokens `success`/`failure` instead of `OK`/`FAIL`, which made praktika render its result as "completed but unknown". Concretely, the [2026-08-13 nightly](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31674904130) reported **green** while the SQLancerPP job had failed on the `WHERE` and `NoREC` oracles. Its per-oracle logs are now attached to their own rows too. ### Testing The scripts' logic was exercised directly, without a real fuzzing run: - `ci/jobs/scripts/sqlancer_failures.py` against **43 real reproducer logs** from a saved SQLancer run: 43 findings → **13 distinct failures**, grouped the way they are actually triaged (PQS memory-limit noise x20, NoREC memory-limit x8, TLPDistinct row-count mismatch x3, TLPSetOp `UNION_DISTINCT` mismatch x1, TLPSetOp NPE x1, CODDTest Code 27 x1, …). Empty and missing log directories yield `no findings` and an empty fragment. - `ci/jobs/sqlancer_job.sh` end to end against stubbed `java`/`wget`/`git`/`mvn`/`clickhouse` binaries: clean run → `OK`, exit 0, 18 console lines; run with findings → `FAIL`, exit 1, 36 console lines and valid nested result JSON; UBSan `runtime error:` → `FAIL` while benign ASan boilerplate stays `OK`; server death, sqlancer crash, missing statistics, runtime-build failure (falls back with a warning), the 50-file upload cap, >10 MB log compression and a deliberately broken analysis script all behave as described. The real verification is the next nightly run of this workflow. ### CI validation (2026-08-14) Validated by dispatching `NightlySQLancer` twice from a throwaway branch on top of this one (short fuzz runs; branch deleted since). **[Run 31825081436](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31825081436) — clean path, 20 min fuzz.** Workflow conclusion `failure`, driven by SQLancerPP (see below). - Docker image with the new Dockerfile built (by this PR's own CI) and reused from the registry here. - Runtime clone + rebuild of `ClickHouse/sqlancer` `main`: **11 s**, commit `3a66cc5ce597`, no fallback (the warm maven repo in the image is doing its job). - **93 oracles** exercised, versus 31 with the old pinned commit. - 4 progress lines on the console for the whole fuzz run; job info `sqlancer main @ 3a66cc5ce597; 56k queries; no findings`; exit 0, job green. - The job's report entry is populated for the first time: status `OK`, `duration: 1243`, the info line and 5 artifact links. For comparison, the same entry in the [2026-08-13 nightly](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/REFs/master/45cb8371bbe63a39f7d0c655543563e8f15e5a40/result_nightlysqlancer.json) is `{"results": [], "links": [], "duration": null}`. - SQLancerPP went `failure` with per-oracle rows (`WHERE`, `QUERY_PARTITIONING` assertions; `FUZZING` → server not responding), each with its logs — and the **workflow status became `FAIL`**. The identical failure reported green on 2026-08-13. **[Run 31830811184](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31830811184) — failure path, 15 min fuzz** with `TextIndexDirectRead` re-included, since it reliably fires on the open ClickHouse#107186. - **37 findings deduplicated into 1 distinct failure**: `TextIndexDirectRead / java.lang.AssertionError / at ClickHouseTextIndexDirectReadOracle.check:95 (x37)`, one report row listing all 37 databases with 10 reproducer logs attached, plus the `Failure analysis` row with `analysis.txt`. - `analysis.txt` per-finding index carries the full assertion for each one (`ClickHouse#107186`, tokenizer, preprocessor, predicate, the diverging key sets and the DDL). - A downloaded reproducer (`database0.log`, 2035 lines) starts with the assertion plus stack trace and ends with the exact `CREATE TABLE ... INDEX idx (s) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha', preprocessor = lower(s))` + `INSERT` that reproduces it. - Job info `39k queries; 37 finding(s) in 1 distinct failure(s)`, job red, workflow `FAIL`. Two fixes came out of this validation and are included: the result-name bug above, and `SQLancerPP` no longer listing per-oracle logs that were never written (praktika replaces the whole job `info` with `WARNING: File [...] was not found`, which buried the result). One observation, not addressed here: the ASan+UBSan server writes ~10 MB of `DB::Exception` stack traces to stderr per 20 minutes (~150 MB projected over 5 h), from logging every failed fuzzer statement at error level. Dropping the mounted `log_level.xml` to `fatal` would remove it while keeping `<Fatal>` and sanitizer detection intact.

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/series
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/series`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus clients** use **`/api/v1/series`** to discover the label sets stored for active series. This endpoint is used by **Prometheus-compatible tools** such as **Grafana** when they need to populate metric and label selectors. ClickHouse **`TimeSeries` tables** can store labels in the main **`tags` Map**, in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**, or in a mixture of both layouts. The endpoint needs to expose the **same logical series** regardless of how those labels are stored. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/series` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint is available through both a **dedicated `/api/v1/series` handler** and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**. It supports **GET requests** and **`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST requests**. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** selects series by metric name and label matchers. Repeated parameters are combined as a **union** and overlapping results are returned only once through **deduplication**. - **`start` and `end`** select series overlapping the requested **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the number of returned series and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Selector parsing:** parse Prometheus series selectors with equality, inequality, regular-expression, and negative regular-expression matchers. - **Storage compatibility:** support metric names, labels in the **`tags` Map**, dedicated tag columns, and mixed rows that use both storage layouts. - **Label normalization:** normalize missing labels to the **Prometheus empty-value semantics** and include the full logical label set in each response. - **PromQL compatibility:** support quoted label names and anchor regular expressions to the **complete label value**. - **Input validation:** validate selectors and timestamps before executing the query. - **Time ranges:** apply the time-range filter when trusted min/max data is available. When it is not available, keep the request valid and return the **compatible candidate superset** allowed by the Prometheus API. - **Result limits:** support zero and positive limits, exact-limit responses, truncation reporting, and invalid-value errors. - **Access control:** read the underlying series metadata through the **`TimeSeries` table-function path** after checking access to the configured **`TimeSeries` table**. Unknown routes are resolved before authorization, so they keep the normal **404 response**. - **Existing endpoints:** apply the configured **`TimeSeries` table access boundary** consistently to the existing Prometheus query endpoints. - **Query lifecycle:** run the generated query through the **normal query pipeline** and keep **query logging** and **query completion handling** intact. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Matcher operators:** metric-name and label selectors with all matcher operators. - **Repeated selectors:** repeated **`match[]`** parameters, selector unions, and overlapping-result deduplication. - **Storage layouts:** Map labels, dedicated tag columns, missing labels, mixed carriers, conflicting carriers, and **`__name__`**. - **Regex and names:** quoted label names and whole-value regular-expression anchoring. - **Selector validation:** invalid and unbounded selectors, including the valid **`{host!~".*"}`** case. - **Time ranges:** two-sided, one-sided, inclusive, and invalid time ranges. - **Min/max behavior:** requests with and without trusted min/max metadata. - **Limits:** zero, exact, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values. - **HTTP methods:** GET and form POST requests. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants**, access checks for all query endpoint families, and unknown-route handling. - **Observability:** query completion records and the existing query API limit behavior. Also ran **Python syntax checks** and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now covers the Prometheus handler configuration and the **`/api/v1/series` endpoint parameters**. ### Stack This is the **base PR** for the follow-up Prometheus API endpoints: - **#114868** adds **`/api/v1/labels`**. - **#114869** adds **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`**.
signals.author: fallintoplace

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/labels
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/labels`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus-compatible clients** use **`/api/v1/labels`** to discover the label names available in matching series. This is useful for **Grafana dashboards**, variable pickers, and integrations that need to build label selectors without fetching every series first. The endpoint follows the same **logical label model** as the series endpoint. It reads labels stored in the **`tags` Map** and in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/labels` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint returns a **sorted, distinct list of label names**. It includes **`__name__`** when at least one matching series exists and supports both **unfiltered discovery** and filtering by matching series. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** filters the series used to build the label-name list. Repeated selectors are combined as a **union**. - **`start` and `end`** restrict the matching series by their **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the returned label names and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Label discovery:** collect distinct names from the canonical metric name, the **`tags` Map**, and configured dedicated tag columns. - **Selector support:** reuse the Prometheus series-selector and matcher behavior from **`/api/v1/series`**. - **Storage compatibility:** support both normal TimeSeries storage and **`tags_to_columns`** layouts while preserving the logical label set. - **Repeated selectors:** combine repeated **`match[]`** parameters without returning duplicate label names. - **Time ranges:** apply trusted min/max bounds when available and keep ranged requests valid with the **approximate superset** behavior allowed by Prometheus when bounds are unavailable. - **Result limits:** support empty, zero, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values, including the Prometheus truncation warning. - **HTTP handling:** support the dedicated endpoint and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**, with endpoint parameters kept separate from ClickHouse settings. - **Access control:** enforce the configured **`TimeSeries` table authorization boundary** before reading the underlying target tables. - **Query lifecycle:** execute through the **normal query pipeline**, preserve query completion handling, and record the request in **`query_log`**. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Label collection:** distinct names, sorted output, **`__name__`**, Map labels, and dedicated columns. - **Selectors:** metric filters, label filters, repeated **`match[]`** unions, and requests with no matching series. - **Time ranges:** matching and non-matching intervals, including empty optional parameters. - **Limits:** truncation warnings and the **`limit`** parameter behavior. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants** on the configured `TimeSeries` table. - **Observability:** successful requests recorded as **`QueryFinish`** entries. - **Shared behavior:** the related Prometheus query and series API regression coverage. Also ran **Python syntax checks**, **XML parsing**, and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now describes the `/api/v1/labels` handler and its supported parameters. ### Stack This PR is **stacked on #114867** and includes the **`/api/v1/series`** changes. After **#114867** merges, this branch can be rebased onto `master`.

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/label/<name>/values
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus-compatible clients** use **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`** to discover the values available for a label. This is used by **Grafana dashboards**, variable pickers, and integrations that need to populate label-value selectors. Prometheus also supports **escaped UTF-8 label names**. The endpoint must decode those names correctly while preserving malformed or intentionally literal values in a predictable way. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/label/<name>/values` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint returns a **sorted, distinct list of values** for one label. It supports metric names through **`__name__`**, labels from the **`tags` Map**, dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**, series selectors, time ranges, and result limits. Supported parameters: - **`<name>`** identifies the label whose values should be returned, including Prometheus **`U__...` escaped names**. - **`match[]`** filters the series contributing values. - **`start` and `end`** restrict the matching series by their **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the returned values and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Value discovery:** return distinct values for ordinary labels and the special **`__name__`** metric-name label. - **Storage compatibility:** read values from the **`tags` Map** and dedicated **`tags_to_columns`** columns using the same logical label semantics as the other metadata endpoints. - **Name decoding:** decode valid Prometheus escaped label names, preserve malformed or overlong escape sequences as literal names, and reject an empty decoded label name. - **Selector support:** filter values by metric and series selectors, including unknown-label and no-match cases. - **Time ranges:** apply trusted min/max bounds when available and keep ranged requests valid with the **approximate superset** behavior allowed by Prometheus when bounds are unavailable. - **Result limits:** support empty, zero, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values, including the Prometheus truncation warning. - **HTTP handling:** add the label-values route to the **combined `/api/v1` handler** and keep endpoint parameters separate from ClickHouse settings. - **Access control:** enforce the configured **`TimeSeries` table authorization boundary** before reading the underlying target tables. - **Query lifecycle:** execute through the **normal query pipeline**, preserve query completion handling, and record the request in **`query_log`**. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Metric names:** values returned through **`__name__`**. - **Label values:** distinct Map values and values from configured dedicated columns. - **Escaped names:** valid UTF-8 decoding, malformed escape sequences, overlong escapes, and empty decoded names. - **Filtering:** selectors, unknown labels, and requests with no matching series. - **Time ranges:** matching and non-matching intervals, including empty optional parameters. - **Limits:** truncation warnings and the maximum valid **UInt64** limit. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants** on the configured `TimeSeries` table. - **HTTP integration:** the main HTTP port, routing, and query completion records. Also ran **Python syntax checks**, **XML parsing**, and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now describes the label-values handler, escaped label names, and its supported parameters. ### Stack This PR is **stacked on #114867** and includes the **`/api/v1/series`** changes. After **#114867** merges, this branch can be rebased onto `master`.

signals.title: Follow-ups for CREATE HANDLER: parse limits of the stored query, docs, refactoring
signals.text: Follow-ups from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 (`CREATE HANDLER`). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 **Requested in review of #106231:** - The two predicates over `IAST::QueryKind` that describe the `readonly` mode - whether a query of that kind is rejected under it, and whether `readonly = 2` still lets it produce side effects - moved out of `SQLDefinedHandlerFromAST` into `Interpreters/QueryKindUnderReadonly.h`; `queryKindRequiresMutatingMethod` is renamed to `isQueryKindRejectedUnderReadonly` after the property it reports. The handler code keeps the statement-level refinements and the HTTP-method fences. - `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` were registered with `IntroducedIn` 26.6 (the development version when they were written); they are released in 26.8. **The one unresolved review finding:** a request could still lower the parse limits of a handler's query. `HTTPHandler::processQuery` relaxed `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` *before* applying the settings the request supplies, and a request names settings freely - so `GET /h?max_parser_depth=1` put the caller's value back and broke a handler the server itself had accepted. The relaxation now happens after the request settings. `max_query_size` had the same hole and did not even need a hostile request: a stored query longer than its default value is creatable and reloadable (both parse without a size limit) but failed on every invocation; it is now raised to fit the query text - not disabled, because `executeQuery` also uses `max_query_size` to decide how much of the request stream to read ahead in search of the query text, where `0` would make it read a single byte. New tests `04897_handler_request_parser_limits` and `04898_handler_large_query_invocation`, both verified to fail without the fix. **Documentation:** the `CREATE HANDLER` page was written into `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/handler.md` - a path in the legacy Docusaurus tree that `9440ca729a3` had already removed - so the only documentation of `CREATE HANDLER` / `ALTER HANDLER` / `DROP HANDLER` was published nowhere. It moves to `docs/reference/statements/create/handler.mdx`, with the frontmatter and internal links converted to that tree's conventions and the page registered in `docs/reference/navigation.json`. `docs/en/operations/system-tables/handlers.md` was a leftover copy of the generated `docs/reference/system-tables/handlers.mdx` whose hand-written `SHOW HANDLERS` / secret-masking paragraph had been lost; that paragraph is restored and the legacy copy deleted. The statement is now cross-referenced from the HTTP interface page, the `DROP` page and the `ALTER` overview, and the anchored (`RE2::FullMatch`) semantics of `URL REGEXP` are documented. Verified locally: all 30 SQL-defined-handler stateless tests pass against a server built from this branch (the 31st match of the `handler` filter, `03354_tcp_handler_async_insert_bug`, is unrelated and needs a writable `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files`), and `04844_handler_deep_query_invocation` still passes without the fix, confirming it covered only the session-level limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed HTTP handler invocation so request-level `max_parser_depth`, `max_parser_backtracks`, and `max_query_size` no longer break stored handler queries, and published the `CREATE HANDLER`, `ALTER HANDLER`, and `DROP HANDLER` documentation.

signals.title: Keep parent `ThreadGroup` alive for child counters
signals.text: Child `ThreadGroup` objects connect their memory and profile counters to parent counters through raw pointers, but did not retain ownership of the parent group. Asynchronous child work could therefore outlive its parent and access destroyed counters. Retain the parent until all child counters have been destroyed. The same CI report exposed that `04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait` runs with a `Replicated` database even though `UNDROP TABLE` is unsupported there. Mark the test accordingly so this configuration skips it. The full release `clickhouse` target builds successfully. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=432b1ae96183f5b085835f4b0aece8d95ce9ce73&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F3%29&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F3%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a segmentation fault in asynchronous work when a child `ThreadGroup` outlives its parent and accesses destroyed memory or profile counters.

signals.title: AI functions: Make quotas per query not per block
signals.text: `AIQuotaTracker` was a stack local inside `executeImpl`, so every block and every pipeline stream started with a fresh allowance. The `ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` and `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query` limits therefore scaled with the data (one allowance per block per function) instead of bounding the query — any limit above the largest block's row count could never fire. The tracker is now a single instance owned by the query `Context` and shared by every AI function call in the query, with atomic counters for the concurrent pipeline threads. The limits now bound the whole query, as their names and documentation state. NOTE: The design decision was made to enforce the quota per-query (one query may have multiple AI function calls) not per-function-call. Enforcing per function call is also possible, but I decided that it doesn't make as much sense especially considering the setting names and the [documentation as currently written](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/ai-function#ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The AI-function quota settings (`ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query`, `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query`) were enforced per block rather than per query, letting a query exceed the configured limit in proportion to the number of blocks and threads processed. They now bound the whole query.

signals.title: Cheaper per-sample add path in timeSeries*ToGrid aggregate functions
signals.text: The `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions pay a fixed cost for every incoming sample in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase`: computing the grid bucket index and looking the bucket up in a hash map. This PR makes both cheaper: - **Int64 fast path for the bucket-index computation.** `bucketIndexForTimestamp` used Int128 division and modulo per sample to stay overflow-safe for adversarial grid parameters. Now, when all grid parameters are bounded by 2^61 (checked once in the constructor; covers every practical case), the per-sample computation runs in plain Int64 arithmetic, dividing by the fixed `step` through a precomputed `libdivide` reciprocal — the `__udivmodti4` calls disappear from query profiles. The Int128 path is kept as-is for out-of-range parameters and single-point grids (`start == end`). - **Cached last-bucket pointer in the batch add loops.** Samples arrive sorted by timestamp within a series, so consecutive samples usually land in the same bucket; the loops now reuse the last bucket pointer and skip the hash-map lookup for same-bucket runs. Inserting into the map can invalidate the cached pointer, but an insert happens only on a bucket change, which re-acquires the pointer. Measured on tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15 s step; scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series, Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3): on a 30-day PromQL `rate` query scanning 69M samples, the per-sample Int128 division (`__udivmodti4`) was ~2% of CPU and the bucket-index computation ~3% — both disappear from the profile with the Int64 fast path; the whole rate-aggregation add path went from ~12% to ~8% of the query. A new performance test `tests/performance/timeseries_to_grid_scalar_add.xml` targets exactly this path: dense scalar samples (40M rows, 200 series, one sample per 15 s) aggregated with `step` = `window` = 300 s, so every in-range sample contributes to exactly one bucket and ~20 consecutive samples land in the same bucket. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up the `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions: per-sample bucket math now avoids Int128 division, and consecutive samples in the same bucket skip the hash-map lookup.

signals.title: Do not abort the server when a loader worker cannot be spawned
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110174 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort that happens when the global thread pool is momentarily saturated while tables are still loading. `AsyncLoader` now keeps running if it cannot spawn an extra loader worker and some worker will still drain the queued jobs, instead of calling `std::terminate`. ### Description `AsyncLoader::spawn` wrapped `scheduleOrThrowOnError` in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose handler is unconditionally `std::terminate()`. A transient `CANNOT_SCHEDULE_TASK` from a saturated global thread pool therefore killed the server (`Received signal 6`) during table loading. Seen 4 times over 4 unrelated PRs and 4 build flavours in 30 days, e.g. [`Stress test (arm_tsan)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108468&sha=27a154474608ee82636207020a9bd13beb8c9449&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), whose stack is `terminate_handler()` -> `std::terminate()` -> `AsyncLoader.cpp:908` `spawn()` -> `:744` `enqueue()`. A spawn must succeed only when nothing else will drain the pool's ready queue, so it now tells three states apart: - a worker that entered `worker()` and is not inside `wait()` drains the queue now; - a worker inside `wait()` on *another* pool's job resumes draining once that job runs; - neither of those means nobody ever will. In the first two cases `spawn` uses the non-throwing `trySchedule`, rolls back its `Pool::workers` increment on failure, warns and returns false. Only the last case keeps the fatal path, byte for byte: the queued jobs would be stranded, and throwing is not an option because `schedule` marks that region non-exception-safe. Covering it needs rollback-and-retry across the loading DAG, out of scope here. All 4 observed rows are recoverable. `BackgroundSchedulePool` narrows the same way (`929227464f9736b`). Two counters are added because `Pool::workers` also counts a worker still queued in the global pool, which drains nothing, and one blocked in `wait()`, which cannot take its own pool's jobs. A saturated pool is remembered so the failing thread creation happens once per episode, not once per queued job, counted by the new `AsyncLoaderSpawnFailures` event; entering `wait()` clears the memo. Tests are gtests asserting which branch was taken, not just that the process survived. A SQL test cannot reach the line: on master the whole call sits under `blockFaultInjections()`. Related: #110174, which removed the mask that hid this exception.

signals.title: TimeSeries: compare consecutive ids via raw columns in getGroupByID
signals.text: The function `timeSeriesIdToGroup` maps time-series ids to per-query group indexes and runs on every scanned row of every transpiled PromQL selector. Its implementation, `ContextTimeSeriesTagsCollector::getGroupByID`, has a fast path for sorted id streams: since samples arrive sorted by id (long runs of equal values), each row is first compared with the previous one, and on equality the previous row's group is reused. That per-row equality check went through a virtual `compareAt` chain (`ColumnTuple` and its two nested columns). This PR makes the fast path compare the raw column data directly for the standard id type `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)`: two integer comparisons per row instead of three virtual calls. Other id types keep the generic `compareAt` path. The standard id type now has a single definition, `standardTimeSeriesIDDataType` in `normalizeTimeSeriesDefinition` (also used where the default id type is resolved); the column check matches against it structurally and asserts the extraction, so a future change of the standard id type cannot silently bypass or desynchronize the fast path. Measured on tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15s step; scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series on a Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3): on a 30-day `rate` query scanning 69M rows, the virtual `compareAt` chain took 10-12% of CPU, reduced to ~4.5% with raw comparisons. The new performance test `tests/performance/timeseries_id_to_group.xml` targets exactly this path: a 40M-row sorted stream of `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` ids in runs of 20000 equal values flows through `timeSeriesIdToGroup`, with the tags collector populated by `timeSeriesStoreTags` in an `IN` subquery, mirroring the shape of transpiled PromQL selectors. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up PromQL queries over `TimeSeries` tables: comparing consecutive time-series ids in `timeSeriesIdToGroup` now uses raw column data instead of virtual per-row comparisons.

signals.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signals.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, despite the request having been made and billed.

signals.title: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database
signals.text: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed table names not being qualified with the default database when a `WITH` alias elsewhere in the same query happened to share the name. `ALTER TABLE other_db.t UPDATE v = (WITH RECURSIVE src AS (SELECT 7 AS id) SELECT max(id) FROM src) + (SELECT max(id) FROM src)` failed with `UNKNOWN_DATABASE`, the same expression through `UPDATE ... SET` silently read the session's `src` instead of `other_db.src`, and a view whose `UNION` branch referenced such a table could not be read from another database. Closes #104972. ### Description `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` records `WITH RECURSIVE` aliases so it does not qualify a name that is a CTE rather than a table. That record was one set shared by the whole visitor instance and never cleared, so an alias declared inside one `SELECT` kept suppressing qualification for every identifier seen afterwards, including a genuine physical table. The leak is forward-only: a colliding name before the CTE is fine. The set becomes a stack of scopes, one pushed per `ASTSelectQuery` and popped by a destructor, so a `SELECT`'s subtree inherits the enclosing aliases and nothing outside it does. Lookups walk it innermost-first. Three cases follow: - The `WITH` list is now walked in the non-recursive case too. A recursive alias is registered before its element is visited, since it may reference itself; a plain alias after, so inside its own definition the name still denotes a table. This mirrors `ApplyWithSubqueryVisitor`, and matters because `ApplyWithGlobalVisitor` copies a first branch's `WITH` list into later `UNION` branches without the `RECURSIVE` flag. - Enclosing scopes are searched for a plain name only when `enable_global_with_statement` is set, matching the resolver: without it the analyzer clears `allow_to_check_cte` for parent scopes. A recursive name is searched unconditionally, since its self-reference resolves inside its own definition. The setting is read per `SELECT`, by replaying the clauses reaching it as `QueryTreeBuilder` does, so a repeated setting takes its last value and `compatibility` is honoured. - `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY QUERY` and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` expand a plain CTE reference into a copy of its body first. Inside that copy the name denotes a table, so that binding is masked. Fixing the visitor covers all 13 construction sites at once. Validated on 40 arms, with eight mutants pinning the scope stack, the clone mask, the registration and lookup order, and the setting handling.

signals.title: Read fresh in-memory metadata at the OPTIMIZE merge-selection read
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104822 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed data loss when a `RENAME COLUMN` runs concurrently with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` on a `MergeTree` table: the merged part could be written with the pre-rename column list, permanently filling the renamed column with its `DEFAULT`. ### Description `26.3`-only fix for issue 80648, authorized in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113929#issuecomment-5229587902. `StorageMergeTree::optimize` calls `merge` synchronously on the query thread, so the merge-selection metadata read runs with a live query context. `MergeTreeData` overrides `getInMemoryMetadataPtr` with a per-query cache that `InterpreterOptimizeQuery` has already populated with the pre-`ALTER` snapshot, so the read returns metadata predating the rename while selection pairs it with parts that already carry the mutation. `MergeTask` takes `storage_columns` from that snapshot and never re-reads, so the merged part keeps the old column list and the renamed column stays `DEFAULT`. Passing `bypass_metadata_cache=true` makes the read honour the invariant the comment above it already states. `scheduleDataProcessingJob` keeps its bare read: its only caller is the background pool, which has no query context, so it already bypasses. `26.4` and later declare the accessor as `(ContextPtr, bool)` with no default, forcing every caller to state a context, so the read is already fresh there. `25.8` has the same bare read but ships `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query` defaulting to `false`. `26.3` is the only supported branch with both the defaulted parameter and that setting `true`, which is why the backport of 104822 compiled unchanged as `getInMemoryMetadataPtr()` and took the cache-consulting path. Validation on two interleaved, load-matched servers built from this tree, setting at its default: base reddens 16 of 7000 iterations against 0 for the fix (Fisher exact p = 3.0e-05); swapping the binaries onto each other's port and data directory keeps the effect with the binary (30/7000 against 0/7000); 80 runner runs of the unmodified `04238_alter_rename_column_merge_race` per arm give 3 base failures with the exact CI signature and 80/80 on the fix. None of the 211 merge and mutation tests with a verdict in both arms regressed.

That PR: Adds a `LeakCheck` parameter to `safeExit` so the three force-exit call sites that run while other threads are alive (`Server.cpp` shutdown, `LocalServer::cleanup`, the client's SIGINT/SIGQUIT handler) skip `__lsan_do_leak_check()`; `Server.cpp` prints a notice, the two client-side ones stay … **1. Client forced-exit on repeated interrupt (`safeExit` in SIGINT handler) untested** `src/Client/ClientApplicationBase.cpp:60` **Risk:** `interruptSignalHandler` -> `ClientBase::tryStopQuery` -> `QueryInterruptHandler::tryStop` (`exit_after_signals.fetch_sub(1) <= 0`) -> `safeExit` at `ClientApplicationBase.cpp:60`. Every existing SIGINT test sends exactly one signal, which leaves `exit_after_signals` at 0 and returns false, so the … **Unique vs PR tests:** The PR's new gtest calls `safeExit` directly with each `LeakCheck` value; the CI python test covers the log-scanner filter. Neither reaches `ClientApplicationBase.cpp:60`, i.e. nothing verifies that the client's interrupt handler still force-exits (and with which status) after the change. cc @groeneai (author of #114053), @alexbakharew (merged/approved #114053) — could you take a look, and add the `can be tested` label if this looks good? ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not applicable — test-only change. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Set the current Keeper component in TextIndexCountSource::generate
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113295 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #113295 `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasAllTokens(str, [...])` is rewritten by the trivial-count-from-text-index optimization into a `ReadFromTextIndexCount` step (added in #111494). Its source runs on a pipeline execution thread: `TextIndexCountSource::generate` -> `computeCountForPart` -> `makeTextIndexInputStream` -> `IMergeTreeDataPart::getStreamNameOrHash(..., IDataPartStorage &)`, whose body probes the part storage with `existsFile`. On a disk that keeps part metadata in Keeper that probe is a real Keeper request, and `Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when no component is set for the scope. `generate()` is the outermost scope this step owns on that thread, and it set none: the step builds its own `Pipe`, so unlike the ordinary read path it never inherits the guard from `MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate`. This adds the one-line RAII guard at the top of `generate()`. The guard is a nesting-safe thread-local stack and every Keeper-reaching call above is a descendant of that scope, so no deeper placement is needed. Same shape as #113295 for `MergeTreeCodecBlockCountsSource::generate` and the sibling `MergeTreeTextIndexSource::generate`. Of the four callers of `makeTextIndexInputStream`, the other three already have an ancestor guard (`MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate` for both `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` sites, the mutate/merge task guards for `MergeTextIndexesTask`); this step was the only gap. Category is `CI Fix or Improvement`, as in #113295 and #113386: the metadata-in-Keeper storage type is registered only under `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts only in debug and sanitizer builds, so this cannot happen in an official stable build. For the same reason no test is added: no public build reaches Keeper through `existsFile`. Validated with the existing `02346_text_index*` suite (plus 50/50 randomized runs of `02346_text_index_optimize_trivial_count`), an `EXPLAIN` assertion that the modified scope is the one the query executes, and a run with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking = 1`. Left alone: the plan-time `getDeserializedFormat` path can also reach `existsFile` for packed skip-index parts and is likewise unguarded, but it predates this step by three weeks and is not this failure's carrier.

signals.title: Fix coordination mode mismatch with a parameterized view subquery
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Coordination mode mismatch for stream <table>: got Default, expected WithOrder` when a parameterized view is used as an `IN`-subquery of an ordered query with parallel replicas enabled. A parameterized view used this way no longer plans its inner read with parallel replicas coordination on a replica. ### Description `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'a')) AND id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'b')) ORDER BY id` with parallel replicas enabled aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds, and threw in release. Root cause. A parameterized view resolves as a `TableFunctionNode`, so its arguments land in `skip_children` in `Planner/CollectSets.cpp` and the view call survives verbatim into the text sent to the replicas. The initiator plans the outer read in order from the sort key and announces `WithOrder`; each replica re-plans the view body, an unordered scan, and announces `Default`. Both key on the bare table name, so the second announcement reaches the first's coordinator and throws. `PlannerJoinTree.cpp` already guards a view planning its own read on a follower, but it compares `table_node` against the chosen `parallel_replicas_table`, and both are null, so it concludes "this is the chosen table" and leaves coordination enabled for the view. A table expression that is not a `TableNode` is now treated as not chosen, which is always correct: `parallel_replicas_table` is a `const TableNode *`, and both walks in `findTableForParallelReplicas` bail out on a table function. The union-children comparison is skipped for the same reason. A view referenced by name is a `TableNode`, so `parallel_replicas_allow_view_over_mergetree = 1` is unaffected. Validation. The test pins the five settings the divergence depends on, three of which the runner randomizes; each of the four that can vary was confirmed load-bearing by a negative control on the unfixed binary. It fails 8 of 8 randomized runs on master with the reported error and passes 100 of 100 here. Expected rows are parallel-replicas-off ground truth, so each query also asserts `ParallelReplicasHandleAnnouncementMicroseconds > 0` to show coordination was reached. The in-tree view, parameterized-view, trivial-view-pushdown and table-function tests are unchanged.

signals.title: Remove the stale TODO about unloading tables in reverse topological order
signals.text: `DatabaseCatalog::checkTableCanBeRemovedOrRenamedUnlocked` skips dependent tables from the same database when the removal comes from `DROP DATABASE`, and carried a TODO asking for the tables to be unloaded in reverse topological order instead. That ordering exists since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057: `InterpreterDropQuery::executeToDatabaseImpl` sorts the tables of a `DROP DATABASE` in reverse loading dependency order, so a dependent is always dropped before the table it depends on. The skip itself is still required, since the dependency graph is consulted per table while the database is being emptied, so only the obsolete TODO is replaced by a pointer to the code that maintains the invariant. Comment-only change. signals.title: Show why a job failed when it never uploaded its own report
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113382 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not user-facing: CI report only. ### Description Two jobs on #113382 lost their runner mid-`Run`, and both report pages render nothing, so the failure looks like a 0-second job with no output: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 praktika did detect the failure and record the reason, but three defects hide it. `_finish_workflow` reported such a job only through `env.add_workflow_error(..., source=result.name)`. `source=` sets the `from` label, not the destination, so the message landed on the workflow node while the job's own node kept an empty `info`, and the page renders notifications from the node it resolved, which is the job. The `Status.ERROR` sites in `runner.py` already call `add_error` on the job's own result; this site did not. A job uploads its own `result_<job>.json` from inside the job, so a job that dies never uploads one and S3 answers 403. The page turned that 403 into "Report does not exist or expired" and returned, discarding the workflow report it had already fetched, which does contain the job's node. That early return is gone, and the cached per-job report is now overwritten on every fetch that came back, so a page polling `sha=latest` cannot keep showing an older commit's node. Rendering that node exposed a third defect, already on master: the auto-reload predicate asked whether the per-job report was running, so a null one read as still loading and the page refetched S3 every 30 seconds forever. It now asks the node the page actually renders. The runner loss is not fixable here and this does not try to. A test drives `_finish_workflow` against a stubbed environment and asserts the reason reaches the uploaded workflow report. For the page, a script extracts the relevant functions from `json.html` and replays the measured S3 responses. Reverting any one fix alone reintroduces its symptom; the healthy and expired paths stay byte-identical.

signals.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signals.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery.

signals.title: Fix server abort on a corrupt ORC stripe footer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114674 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/orc/pull/25 Reading a corrupt ORC blob aborts a debug or sanitizer server instead of raising `INCORRECT_DATA`: ``` generated_message_tctable_lite.cc:228] Check failed: VerifyHasBitConsistency(msg, table) is OK (INTERNAL: Has bits mismatch for Type=orc.proto.StripeFooter Field=1 ``` Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114267&sha=08273e65417c8b6a4fe95d2c2cdad899ea17d041&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29)), and reproduced on pristine master with default settings by `SELECT c0 FROM format(ORC, 'c0 DateTime64(3)', unhex('4f524311...524317'))`, so any user-supplied ORC bytes reach it. **Root cause.** ORC's `DecompressionStream` throws where protobuf's `ZeroCopyInputStream::Next` contract requires a `false` return, so the exception originates inside protobuf's parse loop. `TcParser` keeps has-bits in a register-cached local and writes them back only on its own exit paths, so the unwind skips that write-back and leaves `StripeFooter` with the repeated field `streams` appended to and its has-bit clear. Since the v35.1 protobuf bump the generated destructor checks that invariant, so destroying it aborts. `DebugHardenCheckHasBitConsistency()` gates it on `!NDEBUG` or a sanitizer, so release builds are unaffected, hence a CI fix. **Change.** A submodule bump only. ORC's parse boundary now wraps the caller's stream in an adapter that captures anything escaping `Next`/`BackUp`/`Skip`/`ByteCount`, returns the contract's failure value, and rethrows the original exception once the parser has returned consistent. One header covers all nine `parseProtobufFromStream` call sites, including embedder streams such as ClickHouse's `ORCInputStream`. **Validation.** The blob aborts (RC 134) before the change and afterwards reports `Code: 117 ... Read past EOF in DecompressionStream::readBuffer ... (INCORRECT_DATA)`, byte-identical to master release today, so no user-visible message or code changes. New test `04856_orc_corrupt_stripe_footer` passes 50/50 randomized and fails on the unfixed binary with the has-bits tokens. A 183-case corruption sweep and the full `orc` suite show no behaviour change. `ProtobufZeroCopyInputStreamFromReadBuffer` (Prometheus remote-write) has the same shape, but is unreported and I could not reproduce a failure there, so it is untouched.

signals.title: Reduce merge write amplification in test_rabbitmq_mv_combo
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_rabbitmq_mv_combo` intermittently fails `Time limit of 180 seconds reached` on master, most recently on `amd_msan, 6/8` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%206%2F8%29)). The run is not stalled: consumption strictly increases at every poll, zero no-progress polls. It is too slow because `rabbitmq_max_block_size = 100` makes every consumer flush a 100-row part, so each of the 5 materialized-view targets accumulates ~2,000 level-0 parts and every merge round re-reads the growing `all_1_*` base part - ~300 times over (final merge level 295-316). In the failing job merges read 124M rows to consume the 693k reached before the deadline (~179x); locally, same signature, 122M rows for the full 1M (~122x), ~96% base-part re-reads. This raises `rabbitmq_max_block_size` to 10000 for this test's table only, matching `test_nats_overloaded_insert` (the same high-volume MV fan-out shape). It reduces the work rather than relaxing the budget: the 180s deadline is unchanged and the `parallel_view_processing` setting from #110224 is retained. `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms` stays at 1000, so partial blocks still flush every second - measured block sizes stay between 538 and 6168 rows and never reach the new cap, so the test cannot wait on a full block. The final exact-count assertion is untouched. 10000 is still 52x below the engine default for this table (`max_insert_block_size / rabbitmq_num_consumers`). Validated with 12 interleaved A/B pairs on an MSAN build (the failing configuration, same binary both arms, order alternated). Amplification drops 122.11x -> 12.43x with non-overlapping ranges, and the consumption loop the deadline measures is faster in 12/12 pairs (median 77.2s -> 66.6s). A Debug build cannot show this: there merges use 0.23 of 384 cores, so the amplification is free. 9 tests in the module pass, including `test_rabbitmq_flush_by_block_size`; the other 31 occurrences are unchanged. One residual, not addressed here: the test's `SELECT count() FROM merge(...)` poll still scans rows (~590k per poll) rather than using the trivial-count path. <details> <summary>Per-arm measurements (12 interleaved MSAN pairs)</summary> | metric | base (n=12) | fix (n=12) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | consumption loop (s), median (range) | 77.2 (69.1-81.0) | 66.6 (52.0-71.2) | -13.8% | | merge read amplification (x) | 122.11 (120.51-124.50) | 12.43 (10.90-13.25) | -89.8% | | merge rows read | 122,101,440 | 12,430,342 | -89.8% | | max merge level | 295 (291-301) | 25 (20-27) | -91.5% | | level-0 parts per table | 2000 | 142 (117-152) | -92.9% | Level-0 part size is exactly 100 rows for 9,989 of 9,989 parts before the change; after it, sizes range 538-6168 and reach the 10000 cap in 0 of 2,090 parts. </details>

signals.title: Add a style check for the spelling of `ClickHouse`
signals.text: The product name is written `ClickHouse` - one word, with a capital `C` and a capital `H`. Two case variants are accepted, because a mixed case is unusable there: `clickhouse` for identifiers, package, binary and host names, and `CLICKHOUSE` for macros and environment variables. Everything else - `Clickhouse`, `clickHouse`, `click_house`, `CLICK_HOUSE`, `click-house`, `Click House` - is a misspelling, and until now nothing stopped it from being committed. ## The check The new `clickhouse_spelling` check of the style job searches every file tracked by git, and the file names themselves, in code as well as in comments, messages and documentation. A `git grep -P` prefilter finds the candidate lines (a provable superset of what is reported), so the check costs about a second on a warm page cache and a minute on a cold one. Only the space-separated form is anchored at word boundaries, so an unrelated phrase - "click Household" - is not taken for the product name. The other forms are left unanchored on purpose, so that a misspelling inside a longer identifier - `ClickhouseBuffer` - is reported too. Rather than a long list of excused files, the sources of false positives are handled structurally: * `contrib` - third-party sources. * The generated locale directories of the documentation, `docs/<locale>/` and `docs/snippets/<locale>/`, taken from `docs/gt.config.json`. They are a machine translation of the English pages, so a misspelling there is fixed by fixing the English page; the default locale is not excluded, and `docs/en/` stays enforced. * Release notes - a record of what was published, not edited after the fact. Same pattern as the "new analyzer" wording check in `various_checks.sh`, so the landing and status pages that live next to them stay enforced. * `docs/_specs` - API specifications pinned from their generator by `ci/jobs/cloud_api_docs_nightly.py`. * Regions between `AUTOGENERATED_START` and `AUTOGENERATED_END` markers. Their source of truth - a `FunctionDocumentation` string, for instance - is checked instead, which is what a contributor is supposed to edit. * URLs. A link whose path spells the name differently is not a mistake we can fix, and rewriting it would only break the link. `docs/resources/about/adopters.mdx` alone holds eleven of them. What is left goes into `ci/jobs/scripts/check_style/clickhouse_spelling_ignore.txt`, in the spirit of the existing `experimental_settings_ignore.txt`: a path alone exempts a file, a path followed by a literal exempts only the lines containing that literal. It has fifteen entries, each with the reason next to it, and every one of them is text that is not ours to spell: names defined by other projects (the `ClickhouseClientOptions` of our Azure SDK fork, the `clickHouse*` parameters of Google's Dataflow templates, a third-party client library), verbatim quotations (Stack Overflow post titles shown as query output), and the misspellings that tests feed to the server on purpose - `LIKE` / `ILIKE` case variants, `hasPhrase(message, 'Click House')`, `click_house:` as an unknown URI scheme. ## The fixes The check found 191 misspellings, all fixed here. Most are prose and comments. The renamed identifiers are `isClickhouseApp`, `getClickhouseAttemptNumber` / `setClickhouseAttemptNumber`, `getClickhouseTableSchemaById` / `hasClickhouseTableSchemaById`, the `Clickhouse*` classes of `clickhouse-diagnostics`, the `tabClickhouse` / `btnQueryClickhouse` element ids of the `utils` web tools, and `clickHousePartsInserter.js`, which is renamed. No stale reference to an old name survives - one would be a misspelling, and the check reports those. Three of the fixes are visible to tests, and the first two rely on the server being case-insensitive there, which I confirmed against a running server rather than assumed: * the `X-Clickhouse-Format` HTTP header of `02015_async_inserts_1` - Poco header collections compare names case-insensitively; * the `SOURCE(Clickhouse(...))` dictionary source of `03071_fix_short_circuit_logic` - the parser lowercases the source name (`ExpressionElementParsers.cpp`); * a directory named `Clickhouse` in `03600_disk_app_plain_rewritable_disks_list_cmd`, renamed in the command and in the reference. Its position in the listing is unchanged, since `ClickHouse` sorts before `Cloud` either way. The rule is also written down as item 18 of the `Names` section of the style guide, so a contributor can find it before CI tells them. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Do not run 04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait on database engines without UNDROP support
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56062 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait.sh` has no `# Tags:` line, so the stateless runner admits it into the `--replicated-database` lane. There `InterpreterUndropQuery::executeToTable` rejects the query outright with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` before the busy-wait the test exists to exercise ever starts, so the test's own assertion fires with `UNDROP TABLE was not cancelled with QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED`. Deterministic, not flaky: in that check 1771 of its 1776 `OK` results carry the failure text, against 0 of the 27000+ results in every other check, continuously since the explicit assertion was added on 2026-08-09. It stays invisible because that coverage job relabels diagnosed-flaky results to `OK`; the [master report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=432b1ae96183f5b085835f4b0aece8d95ce9ce73&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F3%29) that exposed it escaped only because a concurrent server death skipped the diagnostics rerun. That relabel is pre-existing and intentional; noted as disclosure, not touched here. `Ordinary` is a second carrier: `DatabaseAtomic` is the only engine that registers dropped tables for undrop, and `Ordinary` does not override `DatabaseOnDisk::dropTable`, so nothing is put into `tables_marked_dropped` and the undrop throws `UNKNOWN_TABLE`. Both rejections verified directly against a server. All three sibling UNDROP tests already tag both engines; 04726 was the only omission. Validation on one binary: the failure reproduces 100% on the pre-fix tree through the real runner; with the tag the test is `SKIPPED` in that lane and under `--db-engine Ordinary`, and still passes in the default `Atomic` lane, 50 of 50 with randomization. Negative controls (tag names typo'd, or the reason comment kept while the `# Tags:` line is deleted) re-admit the test and it fails again, so the tag is load-bearing rather than silently inert. `Related:` is context only; this PR does not implement UNDROP for Replicated. @ alexey-milovidov reached the same conclusion from the same report in PR 114884, which was closed unmerged over its unrelated `ThreadGroup` half, so this tag never landed.

signals.title: Share one referenced input subplan across sibling correlated subqueries
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query plan growing exponentially with the number of correlated subqueries in one expression when `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer` is disabled, which made such a query spend minutes in planning and consume tens of gigabytes. A query with eight sibling correlated subqueries now builds 226 plan steps instead of 6895. ### Description A `WHERE`/`SELECT` expression containing several correlated subqueries decorrelates them one at a time. `addExpressionStep` validates all of them against the header captured *before* that loop, but each subquery referenced the input subplan root as it stood *during* its own iteration, so subquery `k` referenced a subtree already containing subqueries `1..k-1`. When the referenced result is not buffered, the materialization pass clones each referenced root together with the references nested inside it, and the node count doubles per subquery. Measured plan steps for N sibling subqueries (`correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0`): 415 at N = 4 rising to 6895 at N = 8, i.e. exactly `2^N`, reaching 68 GB of resident memory at N = 8. The buffer is also disabled whenever `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'`, so the blow-up is reachable by changing that one setting alone; `make_distributed_plan = 1` forces the buffer off as well (`SettingsQuirks.cpp`). Found as a `Stress test (arm_tsan)` hung check, where a cancelled `INSERT ... SELECT` sat 426 s in plan optimization with 1,670,597 plan nodes (N of about 17, for a `SELECT` repeating one correlated alias 20 times). CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114072&sha=08c0cd1e799e63d9cf42a2402776fa2ce09c9bc7&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 The fix creates one referenced root per expression and reuses it for every sibling. It is used only when the in-memory buffer is not in play, because the buffer optimization replaces the referenced step in place, and only when the shared root's header already carries the subquery's correlated columns. Both cases fall back to today's per-subquery root. After the fix the same plans are 226 steps at N = 8 and grow linearly. The default buffered path is untouched, and results are unchanged over both settings values. Cancellation inside the materialization pass is still not checked; with the plan now linear that pass takes milliseconds, so it is not addressed here.

signals.title: Fix possible crash due to ThreadGroup use-after-free (for async INSERTs/MVs/EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix possible crash due to ThreadGroup use-after-free (for async INSERTs/MVs/EXPLAIN ANALYZE) @filimonov "Borrowed ThreadGroup objects used by materialized view and async insert flush paths point their performance_counters and memory_tracker to the parent query group, so they are valid only while that parent group is alive. Async callbacks could capture such a borrowed group and later attach it on a pool thread after the parent query group had finished." Eventually we have to store parent's `ThreadGroupPtr` to account things properly, initial fix #108988 tries to avoid this, but this breaks propagating counters to queries Thanks to @filimonov for original fix https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108988 This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109891 it became too complex <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1471` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
