signal.title: Implement PromQL range functions present_over_time, absent_over_time, quantile_over_time and predict_linear
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented range functions `present_over_time()`, `absent_over_time()`, `quantile_over_time()` and `predict_linear()`. ### Description Implements four PromQL functions over range vectors that were previously rejected with a not-implemented error: - `present_over_time(v range-vector)` — for each grid point, `1` if its staleness window contains at least one sample, otherwise the series is dropped. - `absent_over_time(v range-vector)` — an empty vector if the range vector has any samples, otherwise a 1-element synthetic series with value `1` and the labels inferred from the selector's equality matchers (matching Prometheus `absent_over_time` / `absent` semantics). - `quantile_over_time(phi scalar, v range-vector)` — the φ-quantile of the sample values in each grid point's window, computed with the R-7 (inclusive) method (`quantileExactInclusive`). φ outside `[0, 1]` yields ±Inf and NaN φ yields NaN, as in Prometheus. - `predict_linear(v range-vector, t scalar)` — simple linear regression over the in-window samples, extrapolated `t` seconds past the evaluation time. **Implementation** - Two new grid aggregate functions: - `timeSeriesPresentToGrid` — `1` if a window has any sample, else `NULL`. - `timeSeriesQuantileToGrid` — R-7 inclusive quantile over a window (non-invertible summary that collects window values and sorts them in `getResult`). Both are registered inline in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesHelpers.cpp`. `predict_linear` reuses the existing `timeSeriesPredictLinearToGrid` aggregate (the `is_predict` variant of the linear-regression aggregate). - `present_over_time` is wired through `applyFunctionOverRange`'s `impl_map`. `quantile_over_time` and `predict_linear` have dedicated translators because they take an extra scalar argument. - `absent_over_time` builds a per-series presence grid via `present_over_time`, then at runtime counts present series per grid point (`countForEach`) and inverts the result, so it works whether or not the metric exists (a selector on a missing metric is a runtime subquery, not a compile-time-empty one). Output labels are derived from the selector's matchers, like `absent()`. No parser changes were needed — the grammar already accepts these function names and `getFunctionResultType` already returns the correct result types. **Testing**: new parser cases in `gtest_PromQLParser.cpp` for `present_over_time` and `absent_over_time` (`quantile_over_time` / `predict_linear` were already covered); new stateless test `04551_promql_phase3_range_functions.sh` exercising all four functions (present/absent, quantile at φ = 0 / 0.5 / 1, predict_linear at offsets 0 and 60) against a multi-series TimeSeries table, with values verified against Prometheus semantics. **Update: time-varying `predict_offset` / `phi`** `predict_linear`'s `t` and `quantile_over_time`'s `phi` now also accept a per-grid-point-varying PromQL scalar (e.g. `time()` in a range query), not just a constant or single-row scalar. This is handled by two new, self-contained aggregate functions, `timeSeriesPredictLinearVaryingToGrid` / `timeSeriesQuantileVaryingToGrid`, which take the varying value as a 3rd `Array(Float64)` argument instead of a fixed aggregate parameter (ClickHouse aggregate parameters are bound once per instance and can't vary per row). They're isolated from `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase` (shared by ~10 other `timeSeries*ToGrid` functions) to avoid regression risk to those. Since these are public SQL aggregate functions, not just an internal translator detail, they validate that the 3rd-argument array is identical across every row/merged state and throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` otherwise, rather than silently using whichever array was seen first. **Scope note**: the varying value is normalized to `Array(Float64)` in the translator so it works for `Float32`-valued `TimeSeries` tables too, not just `Float64`. However, the PromQL scalar's *own* grid representation (`fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s `SCALAR_GRID` output for `time()`) is cast to `Array(scalar_data_type)`, which is the *table's value type* — for a `Float32`-valued table, that means `time()`'s own raw values (Unix timestamps, ~1.7e9) already lose precision (~128-unit rounding at that magnitude) before my code ever sees them. This is a pre-existing property of `scalar_data_type` being shared between value-precision and timestamp-scalar-precision, not something this change introduces, but this change is what makes it reachable for `predict_offset`/`phi`. It only matters when the varying value is derived from a large absolute number (like raw `time()`) on a `Float32` table; typical `phi` (`[0, 1]`) or `predict_offset` (seconds-scale) formulas aren't affected. Fixing the root cause would mean changing `fromFunctionTime.cpp`'s shared `SCALAR_GRID` representation, which has ~15 other callers — out of scope here.

signal.title: Sampling via geometric distribution
signal.text: Attempt to implement sampling via geometric distribution (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85195) ```sql SET allow_experimental_bernoulli_sample = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_bench; CREATE TABLE t_bench (x UInt64, payload String DEFAULT randomString(200)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS index_granularity = 256; -- 50M rows × ~208 bytes = 10 GB uncompressed. -- 50M / 256 = 195312 granules. At p=0.001, ~22.6% hits INSERT INTO t_bench (x) SELECT number FROM numbers(50000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE t_bench FINAL; SELECT 'parts:', count(), 'total_rows:', sum(rows) FROM system.parts WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_bench' AND active; TRUNCATE TABLE system.query_log; SYSTEM DROP MARK CACHE; SYSTEM DROP UNCOMPRESSED CACHE; SYSTEM DROP FILESYSTEM CACHE; SELECT 'sampled scan'; SELECT count(), sum(cityHash64(payload)) FROM t_bench SAMPLE 0.001 SETTINGS bernoulli_sample_seed = 42; SYSTEM DROP MARK CACHE; SYSTEM DROP UNCOMPRESSED CACHE; SYSTEM DROP FILESYSTEM CACHE; SELECT 'full scan'; SELECT count(), sum(cityHash64(payload)) FROM t_bench; SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS; SELECT 'query_log results (raw values)'; SELECT query_duration_ms AS ms, read_rows, read_bytes, formatReadableSize(read_bytes) AS bytes_h, replaceRegexpOne(query, '\\s+SETTINGS.*', '') AS q FROM system.query_log WHERE current_database = currentDatabase() AND query LIKE '%FROM t_bench%' AND query NOT LIKE '%query_log%' AND query NOT LIKE '%system%' AND type = 'QueryFinish' ORDER BY event_time_microseconds; DROP TABLE t_bench; ┌──ms─┬─read_rows─┬──read_bytes─┬─bytes_h──┬─q──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 1. │ 176 │ 11272960 │ 1853847797 │ 1.73 GiB │ SELECT count(), sum(cityHash64(payload)) FROM t_bench SAMPLE 0.001 │ 2. │ 262 │ 50000000 │ 10150000000 │ 9.45 GiB │ SELECT count(), sum(cityHash64(payload)) FROM t_bench; │ └─────┴───────────┴─────────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Experimental. Allow `SAMPLE` clause on `MergeTree` tables without a `SAMPLE BY` key using Bernoulli row-level sampling. Enable with `SET allow_experimental_bernoulli_sample = 1`. Each row is independently selected with the given probability, and entire granules with no sampled rows are skipped. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. signal.title: group_by_each_block_no_merge setting
signal.text: ### Changelog category: - New Feature ### Changelog entry: Added the `group_by_each_block_no_merge` setting (off by default). When enabled, a query with `GROUP BY` is processed in a streaming fashion: aggregation is performed, finalized, and flushed for every block of data, without fully merging the partial results. The exact output is plan-dependent and not deterministic in general. This is intended for special cases such as populating a materialized view with `POPULATE`, where the partial results are merged later in the background. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/9604 ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) The setting is documented in `src/Core/Settings.cpp` (rendered into the settings reference). > Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/

signal.title: Fix logical error in optimize_or_like_chain with aggregate/window function on LIKE LHS
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Function node with name '...' is not resolved as ordinary function`) that could occur with `optimize_or_like_chain` enabled when an aggregate or window function appeared on the left-hand side of a `LIKE`/`ILIKE`/`match` inside an `OR` chain. ### Description Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (STID 3477-117d) on [this CI run](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107567&sha=16ccfffe167f14e51996ce4ec16384f92e4d15d0&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29). Not caused by that PR — it is a trunk analyzer bug the fuzzer happened to surface there. `isExpressionNonDeterministic` in `ConvertOrLikeChainPass` guarded its `getFunctionOrThrow()` call with `FunctionNode::isResolved()`. `isResolved()` returns true for aggregate and window functions too (it only checks that the function pointer is set), but `getFunctionOrThrow()` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the function kind is not `ORDINARY`. So a resolved aggregate (e.g. `count()`) or window function nested under a `LIKE` argument in an `OR` chain tripped the assertion — an exception in release builds, an abort in debug/sanitizer builds. Fix: guard with `isOrdinaryFunction()` instead, matching the existing correct guard in `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`. Aggregate/window functions are never non-deterministic-in-scope-of-query at this point, so recursing into their children is sufficient. Minimal reproducer (aborts before the fix on a debug build): ```sql SET optimize_or_like_chain = 1; SELECT toString(count()) LIKE '%1%' OR toString(count()) LIKE '%2%' FROM numbers(3); ``` Covered by `tests/queries/0_stateless/04545_optimize_or_like_chain_aggregate_lhs.sql` (aggregate and window variants, plus an ordinary-function control that must still collapse).

signal.title: Allow multiple key condition atoms per predicate leaf
signal.text: If we have, ```sql CREATE TABLE test ( dt DateTime ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (toYYYYMM(dt), toDate(dt), toStartOfHour(dt), dt) SETTINGS index_granularity = 1; INSERT INTO test SELECT toDateTime('2026-01-01 00:00:00') + number * 3600 FROM numbers(24 * 40); ``` Then, for query such as: ```sql EXPLAIN indexes = 1 SELECT count() FROM test WHERE dt = toDateTime('2026-01-10 00:00:00'); ``` Currently, we use only one primary key column: ```response Keys: dt Condition: (dt in [1768003200, 1768003200]) Parts: 1/1 Granules: 960/960 ``` PR will use all the keys applicable: ```response Keys: toYYYYMM(dt) toDate(dt) toStartOfHour(dt) dt Condition: and((toStartOfHour(dt) in [1768003200, 1768003200]), and((toDate(dt) in [20463, 20463]), and((toYYYYMM(dt) in [202601, 202601]), (dt in [1768003200, 1768003200])))) Parts: 1/1 Granules: 2/960 ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow each predicate leaf to use all applicable primary key expressions for pruning. For example, if the primary key is `toYYYYMMDD(dt), toDate(dt), dt` and the filter condition is `WHERE dt >= toDateTime('2026-01-10 00:00:00')`, ClickHouse will be able to use all three primary key expressions to prune as much as possible, instead of currently using only one of them. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/33056. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/99960. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Fix coordination mode mismatch with a parameterized view subquery
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Coordination mode mismatch for stream <table>: got Default, expected WithOrder` when a parameterized view is used as an `IN`-subquery of an ordered query with parallel replicas enabled. A parameterized view used this way no longer plans its inner read with parallel replicas coordination on a replica. ### Description `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'a')) AND id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'b')) ORDER BY id` with parallel replicas enabled aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds, and threw in release. Root cause. A parameterized view resolves as a `TableFunctionNode`, so its arguments land in `skip_children` in `Planner/CollectSets.cpp` and the view call survives verbatim into the text sent to the replicas. The initiator plans the outer read in order from the sort key and announces `WithOrder`; each replica re-plans the view body, an unordered scan, and announces `Default`. Both key on the bare table name, so the second announcement reaches the first's coordinator and throws. `PlannerJoinTree.cpp` already guards a view planning its own read on a follower, but it compares `table_node` against the chosen `parallel_replicas_table`, and both are null, so it concludes "this is the chosen table" and leaves coordination enabled for the view. A table expression that is not a `TableNode` is now treated as not chosen, which is always correct: `parallel_replicas_table` is a `const TableNode *`, and both walks in `findTableForParallelReplicas` bail out on a table function. The union-children comparison is skipped for the same reason. A view referenced by name is a `TableNode`, so `parallel_replicas_allow_view_over_mergetree = 1` is unaffected. Validation. The test pins the five settings the divergence depends on, three of which the runner randomizes; each of the four that can vary was confirmed load-bearing by a negative control on the unfixed binary. It fails 8 of 8 randomized runs on master with the reported error and passes 100 of 100 here. Expected rows are parallel-replicas-off ground truth, so each query also asserts `ParallelReplicasHandleAnnouncementMicroseconds > 0` to show coordination was reached. The in-tree view, parameterized-view, trivial-view-pushdown and table-function tests are unchanged.

signal.title: Reduce merge write amplification in test_rabbitmq_mv_combo
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_rabbitmq_mv_combo` intermittently fails `Time limit of 180 seconds reached` on master, most recently on `amd_msan, 6/8` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%206%2F8%29)). The run is not stalled: consumption strictly increases at every poll, zero no-progress polls. It is too slow because `rabbitmq_max_block_size = 100` makes every consumer flush a 100-row part, so each of the 5 materialized-view targets accumulates ~2,000 level-0 parts and every merge round re-reads the growing `all_1_*` base part - ~300 times over (final merge level 295-316). In the failing job merges read 124M rows to consume the 693k reached before the deadline (~179x); locally, same signature, 122M rows for the full 1M (~122x), ~96% base-part re-reads. This raises `rabbitmq_max_block_size` to 10000 for this test's table only, matching `test_nats_overloaded_insert` (the same high-volume MV fan-out shape). It reduces the work rather than relaxing the budget: the 180s deadline is unchanged and the `parallel_view_processing` setting from #110224 is retained. `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms` stays at 1000, so partial blocks still flush every second - measured block sizes stay between 538 and 6168 rows and never reach the new cap, so the test cannot wait on a full block. The final exact-count assertion is untouched. 10000 is still 52x below the engine default for this table (`max_insert_block_size / rabbitmq_num_consumers`). Validated with 12 interleaved A/B pairs on an MSAN build (the failing configuration, same binary both arms, order alternated). Amplification drops 122.11x -> 12.43x with non-overlapping ranges, and the consumption loop the deadline measures is faster in 12/12 pairs (median 77.2s -> 66.6s). A Debug build cannot show this: there merges use 0.23 of 384 cores, so the amplification is free. 9 tests in the module pass, including `test_rabbitmq_flush_by_block_size`; the other 31 occurrences are unchanged. One residual, not addressed here: the test's `SELECT count() FROM merge(...)` poll still scans rows (~590k per poll) rather than using the trivial-count path. <details> <summary>Per-arm measurements (12 interleaved MSAN pairs)</summary> | metric | base (n=12) | fix (n=12) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | consumption loop (s), median (range) | 77.2 (69.1-81.0) | 66.6 (52.0-71.2) | -13.8% | | merge read amplification (x) | 122.11 (120.51-124.50) | 12.43 (10.90-13.25) | -89.8% | | merge rows read | 122,101,440 | 12,430,342 | -89.8% | | max merge level | 295 (291-301) | 25 (20-27) | -91.5% | | level-0 parts per table | 2000 | 142 (117-152) | -92.9% | Level-0 part size is exactly 100 rows for 9,989 of 9,989 parts before the change; after it, sizes range 538-6168 and reach the 10000 cap in 0 of 2,090 parts. </details>

signal.title: keeper: Increase default `write_snapshot_version` to 8 and make it hot-reloadable
signal.text: Version 6 is a bit of a ticking bomb as it stops working after 2^31 requests. Hot-reloading helps in this scenario: * `write_snapshot_version` is 6 (writes 31-bit sequence numbers for znodes) * some znode's sequence number grows above 2^31, and the server stops writing snapshots but otherwise stays fully functional, * you don't notice for a week * then you notice and want to increase `write_snapshot_version` to 7 * you increase+restart one server * but there's a week's worth of log entries for this server to catch up on, so it takes forever to catch up * until it catches up you can't restart other servers without losing availability * you're stuck, oops With this you can change the setting in the config file without restarting servers, so the valuable accumulated in-memory state gets snapshotted and not lost. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required)

signal.title: Add file IO and integrate new keeper storage
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Keeper can store data on disk now, in a custom LSM tree. It has similar performance to the previous storage. Use coordnation setting `use_new_storage = true` to enable, `storage_memory_only = false` to store files on disk, add `data_storage_path` or `data_storage_disk` to config to specify where to put the files. To write to S3, point `data_storage_disk` to a disk of type `s3_plain`. --- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107261 added new storage with memory-only mode. This PR * Adds ability to store data in files. The storage is not actually persistent, the directory is wiped on startup and re-created from snapshot, just like with previous rocksdb storage. So the files don't have things like headers and version numbers yet, we can add that later if we want faster startup. * Integrates the new storage into keeper. (This PR replaces https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112378 )

signal.title: Implement geo-location awareness during fetching
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): - Implement geo-location awareness during fetching This PR try to solve the issue in #52398. When you have a cross-ocean ClickHouse deployment and each region has multiple ClickHouse replicas, the cross-ocean network bandwidth could become expensive. For example, you have two replicas in `US` and two replicas in `APAC`, once you insert data to a replica in `APAC`, both `US` replicas will try to fetch parts from the `APAC` node, which double the necessary cross-ocean network bandwidth. We introduce a new component, `ReplicatedMergeTreeGeoReplicationController` that enable the following replication architecture: ``` US1 (region leader) <-----------------------> APAC1 (region leader) | | US2 (follower) APAC2 (follower) ``` Each region will have a regional leader and multiple followers. During replication, all replicas still pull log entries from ZooKeeper log queue to its queue, no matter which replica publish the entry. However, when replaying the log entries, if fetching needed, following constraints will apply: 1. A region leader can fetch part from any replica (inside and outside of the region) 2. A follower can only fetch part from the leader If the target part is not ready on the leader, followers will defer execution of the log entry (default 20 seconds). If a follower waits for a leader for too long (default 900 seconds), it will stop waiting and try to fetch on any replica (or check if the part is broken). The leader is per-table. After being elected, the leader will maintain a _lease_ in ZooKeeper, so other node know that there is a leader. All replicas within a region will run leader election if leader is absented (currently leader election is done with ZooKeeper). Additional ZooKeeper nodes per replicated table: - `/path_to_table/regions/{region}` - `/path_to_table/regions/{region}/leader_election`: leader election node for the region `region` - `/path_to_table/regions/{region}/leader_lease`: ephemeral node, current leader of the region - `/path_to_table/replicas/{replica}/{$REGION}`: ephemeral node, ZooKeeper information about the region of current replica You can enable this feature by setting `geo_replication_control_region` when create replicated table. ```xml <clickhouse> <replicated_merge_tree> <geo_replication_control_region>APAC</geo_replication_control_region> <!-- values defined by user --> </replicated_merge_tree> </clickhouse> ``` ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. signal.title: Improve table creation under database iceberg (Iceberg Rest catalog).
signal.text: Improve the performance of table creation under database iceberg. - Before: tons of seconds. - After: sub seconds. `RestCatalog::createNamespaceIfNotExists` calls `/v1/{prefix}/namespaces` to create a new namespace. The service will throw HTTP error `409 Conflicts` if the namespace already exists. And the HTTP client will retry the call 10 times which consume plenty of time. This PR makes the HTTP client not retry `409 Conflicts` errors. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up table creation in the `Iceberg` REST catalog by treating the HTTP `409 Conflict` response ("namespace already exists") as non-retriable, so repeated `CREATE TABLE` statements in an existing namespace no longer wait through the HTTP retry backoff. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. signal.title: Cheaper per-sample add path in timeSeries*ToGrid aggregate functions
signal.text: The `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions pay a fixed cost for every incoming sample in `AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase`: computing the grid bucket index and looking the bucket up in a hash map. This PR makes both cheaper: - **Int64 fast path for the bucket-index computation.** `bucketIndexForTimestamp` used Int128 division and modulo per sample to stay overflow-safe for adversarial grid parameters. Now, when all grid parameters are bounded by 2^61 (checked once in the constructor; covers every practical case), the per-sample computation runs in plain Int64 arithmetic, dividing by the fixed `step` through a precomputed `libdivide` reciprocal — the `__udivmodti4` calls disappear from query profiles. The Int128 path is kept as-is for out-of-range parameters and single-point grids (`start == end`). - **Cached last-bucket pointer in the batch add loops.** Samples arrive sorted by timestamp within a series, so consecutive samples usually land in the same bucket; the loops now reuse the last bucket pointer and skip the hash-map lookup for same-bucket runs. Inserting into the map can invalidate the cached pointer, but an insert happens only on a bucket change, which re-acquires the pointer. Measured on tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15 s step; scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series, Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3): on a 30-day PromQL `rate` query scanning 69M samples, the per-sample Int128 division (`__udivmodti4`) was ~2% of CPU and the bucket-index computation ~3% — both disappear from the profile with the Int64 fast path; the whole rate-aggregation add path went from ~12% to ~8% of the query. A new performance test `tests/performance/timeseries_to_grid_scalar_add.xml` targets exactly this path: dense scalar samples (40M rows, 200 series, one sample per 15 s) aggregated with `step` = `window` = 300 s, so every in-range sample contributes to exactly one bucket and ~20 consecutive samples land in the same bucket. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up the `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions: per-sample bucket math now avoids Int128 division, and consecutive samples in the same bucket skip the hash-map lookup.

signal.title: TimeSeries: compare consecutive ids via raw columns in getGroupByID
signal.text: The function `timeSeriesIdToGroup` maps time-series ids to per-query group indexes and runs on every scanned row of every transpiled PromQL selector. Its implementation, `ContextTimeSeriesTagsCollector::getGroupByID`, has a fast path for sorted id streams: since samples arrive sorted by id (long runs of equal values), each row is first compared with the previous one, and on equality the previous row's group is reused. That per-row equality check went through a virtual `compareAt` chain (`ColumnTuple` and its two nested columns). This PR makes the fast path compare the raw column data directly for the standard id type `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)`: two integer comparisons per row instead of three virtual calls. Other id types keep the generic `compareAt` path. The standard id type now has a single definition, `standardTimeSeriesIDDataType` in `normalizeTimeSeriesDefinition` (also used where the default id type is resolved); the column check matches against it structurally and asserts the extraction, so a future change of the standard id type cannot silently bypass or desynchronize the fast path. Measured on tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15s step; scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series on a Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3): on a 30-day `rate` query scanning 69M rows, the virtual `compareAt` chain took 10-12% of CPU, reduced to ~4.5% with raw comparisons. The new performance test `tests/performance/timeseries_id_to_group.xml` targets exactly this path: a 40M-row sorted stream of `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` ids in runs of 20000 equal values flows through `timeSeriesIdToGroup`, with the tags collector populated by `timeSeriesStoreTags` in an `IN` subquery, mirroring the shape of transpiled PromQL selectors. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up PromQL queries over `TimeSeries` tables: comparing consecutive time-series ids in `timeSeriesIdToGroup` now uses raw column data instead of virtual per-row comparisons.

signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Allow to POST data to the HTTP server from a subquery and receive the result for URL table function - Motivation: This is a necessary feature for use cases of URL table function which require some body content - Parameters: Now `url` function may receive a new argument `body`. This might a simple quoted string or arbitrary subquery - `body` parameters is ought to have 1 or 2 arguments `body(input_source, format)`: 1. `input_source` is either a constant expression or a subquery. Subquery would be executed an the result would be used to construct the body payload. 2. `format` is an optional argument indicating how `input_source` data should be used for payload. The probably most common would be `JSONLines` and it is used as a default one. This argument is ignored in case `input_source` is not a subquery, but a constant expression - Example use: Just a string as a body parameter ```sql SELECT * FROM url('https://slack.com/api/users.info', JSONLines, headers('Content-Type', 'application/json', 'Authorization', '<your auth header>'), body('{"user":"'..."}')) ``` Subquery result a body parameter. signal.title: Do not consult the query context when building a CAST
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR: Context has expired` exception when a stored expression containing `accurateCastOrDefault` or a `to<Type>OrDefault` function is evaluated after the query that created it has finished, for example a `MATERIALIZED` column default on `INSERT` or a mutation expression. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 `CastOverloadResolverImpl` inherited `WithContext`, which holds only a `weak_ptr<const Context>`, and its `buildImpl` passed `getContext()` to `createFunctionBaseCast`. That is safe only during analysis, while a caller still holds a strong `ContextPtr`. #109946 made `FunctionCastOrDefault` store that resolver as a member and call `build()` at execute time. The `ActionsDAG` keeps the resolver alive but nothing keeps its context alive, and both affected paths build the DAG from a function-local `Context::createCopy` that dies on return (`inplaceBlockConversions.cpp:230` for materialized-column defaults, `MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1762` for mutations). Evaluating such an expression later throws `Context has expired`: an exception in release builds, a server abort under debug and sanitizers. This captures the conversion settings in the resolver's constructor, while the context is provably alive, and has `buildImpl` consume that snapshot. `FunctionCast` used its `ContextPtr` for nothing but `settings(context, ...)`, so the snapshot moves one step earlier in the same call chain rather than being introduced. The resolver now holds no context at all, so the `WithContext` exception for this file in `various_checks.sh` is removed. The two build paths keep their distinct `DateTimeOverflowBehavior`: `Saturate` for `createInternalCast`, `Ignore` for `buildImpl`. Sharing one snapshot between them would silently change date-time conversion. Since a snapshot replaces a live context, every context-derived conversion setting was compared before and after and is byte-identical, including all three `date_time_overflow_behavior` modes, `cast_keep_nullable`, `precise_float_parsing`, the IPv4/IPv6 error settings and timezone substitution. `04510_accurateCastOrDefault_settings` from #109946 passes unchanged. The new test aborts a master server at `CastOverloadResolver.cpp:195` and passes with this change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. The defect rides along with #109946, so it is present wherever that landed: 26.7 (#114689, merged); the 25.8, 26.3 and 26.5 backports are still open. <details> <summary>CI provenance</summary> `Logical error: Context has expired`, STID `1805-460a`, first seen 2026-08-13 22:45:16 UTC, about four hours after #109946 merged. The frame pair `CastOverloadResolverImpl::buildImpl` + `Context has expired` has no earlier occurrence in the 90 days CIDB retains. | when (UTC) | check | where | |---|---|---| | 2026-08-14 02:20:39 | [Stress test (arm_release)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=17d2798b962607ded301a9cab913c8ca70a33409&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29) | master, `17d2798b9626` | | 2026-08-14 01:49:18 | [AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114666&sha=dc79add25489c923c36b67be101b349bb964b190&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-14 00:02:12 | [Stress test (amd_tsan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114131&sha=06852ededde08f411d205aea05f6a78dbadaf55c&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-13 22:50:06 | [AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100374&sha=50f4e25e8e3204407e724392592231c2ac54151c&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29) | unrelated PR | | 2026-08-13 22:45:16 | [AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112679&sha=a2d3810c4df7a6d108a1a5b207e779cc41ae7e86&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29) | unrelated PR | The master row is bucketed as STID `1805-4810` because an STID is a stack hash, but it carries both discriminating frames and `17d2798b9626` contains #109946. </details>

signal.title: Add ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE to change a MergeTree-family table's engine
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE = ...MergeTree(...)` to change the engine of a MergeTree-family table in place (for example `MergeTree` into `ReplacingMergeTree` or `SummingMergeTree`). Gated behind the experimental setting `allow_experimental_alter_modify_engine`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107481 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov. `ALTER TABLE t MODIFY ENGINE = <engine>` changes a MergeTree-family table's engine in place. Only the merge semantics (`MergingParams`) change: columns, keys and settings are kept, and data is not rewritten. Existing parts re-merge under the new semantics via background merges and `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`, as with the part-level reset in #107481. A new `MODIFY_ENGINE` alter command rewrites the engine clause in the CREATE query (`StorageInMemoryMetadata::new_engine` -> `applyMetadataChangesToCreateQuery`); `MergingParams::parseFromEngineAST` builds and validates the new merge params against the columns and final settings, so a rejection never leaves an unloadable CREATE on disk. Supported targets: `Replacing`, `Summing`, `Aggregating`, `Collapsing`, `VersionedCollapsing`, `Coalescing`, `Graphite`. A required column may be added in the same statement, before `MODIFY ENGINE`. Non-replicated tables only; old-syntax tables are rejected, their keys being positional engine arguments. Because data is not rewritten, a transition is refused when existing parts could not satisfy the target's invariants: a nullable or unreadable `Graphite` path/time column (the rollup reads them with `getDataAt`/`getUInt`), and `VersionedCollapsing` with the version column outside the sorting key, whose reload widens the key under existing parts. **Two questions for review:** 1. Reload-only, rather than a live swap: `merging_params` is read lock-free from hot paths and often bound by const reference for a whole query, and an exclusive lock cannot be taken there (the query holds `drop_lock` in read mode). An immediate swap needs either a `MultiVersion` `merging_params` or recreating the storage. Which do you prefer? 2. The coordinated `Replicated*MergeTree` switch (decision 3 on the issue) is not implemented. `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` already persists the merge mode, so that is the natural next step. Tests: `04340_alter_modify_engine` (the gate, each transition's merge semantics under `FINAL`, the validation errors, the AST JSON round trip), `04341_alter_modify_engine_access` and `04342_alter_modify_engine_replicated`. Docs: `docs/reference/statements/alter/engine.mdx`.

signal.title: Do not let a post-run coverage diagnostic discard a finished test run's exit code
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `NightlyCoverage` shards exit 1 after every test has already passed. CIDB gets a pseudo-test row `clickhouse-test` / FAIL whose whole context is `clickhouse-test exited with code 1`, while the report shows the shard `OK` with `Failed: 0`. On master: 83 such rows in 30 days, 26 nights, all 8 shards, 6 of them on one nightly. Cause: `main()`'s post-run coverage block printed one diagnostic line built from two `FINAL` aggregates over `system.coverage_log`, the only two statements in that block outside a `try/except`. `clickhouse_execute` defaults to `timeout=30` and re-raises after 5 retries, and the aggregates sit at that cap: the job's own exporter runs the same aggregate over the same 23.4-25.4M rows in 20-29s. The `TimeoutError` propagates out of `main()`, so `sys.exit(exit_code.value)` never runs and Python exits 1 with every result already collected. That costs a red job for a non-failure, and an exit status that no longer separates a test failure from a teardown timeout. The statement is deleted rather than guarded because in this job it is a vestigial duplicate: `CoverageExporter.do()` re-runs the identical aggregate about 30s later, prints a strict superset of the numbers, and raises when the row count is zero. Nothing reads `cov_rows`/`cov_tests`. A local run drops the export stage, so it loses the line rather than seeing it duplicated. Validated locally: the extracted block exits 1 before the change and 0 after, with negative controls confirming the probe is specific to this timeout. Every remaining `clickhouse_execute` in the post-run block is now guarded (checked by AST). The pre-run block is untouched: it is meant to fail the run when coverage is broken. Two siblings are left alone: `coverage_indirect_calls` is redundant the same way but already guarded, and `reportCoverage` is unguarded but no CI job passes `--report-coverage`. CI report, shard 3/8 of the 2026-08-13 nightly: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=3da3cf323b91553960bdf55780a3b94e9deb5793&name_0=NightlyCoverage&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage_per_test%2C%20per_test_coverage%2C%203%2F8%29

signal.title: Set the current Keeper component in TextIndexCountSource::generate
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113295 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #113295 `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasAllTokens(str, [...])` is rewritten by the trivial-count-from-text-index optimization into a `ReadFromTextIndexCount` step (added in #111494). Its source runs on a pipeline execution thread: `TextIndexCountSource::generate` -> `computeCountForPart` -> `makeTextIndexInputStream` -> `IMergeTreeDataPart::getStreamNameOrHash(..., IDataPartStorage &)`, whose body probes the part storage with `existsFile`. On a disk that keeps part metadata in Keeper that probe is a real Keeper request, and `Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when no component is set for the scope. `generate()` is the outermost scope this step owns on that thread, and it set none: the step builds its own `Pipe`, so unlike the ordinary read path it never inherits the guard from `MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate`. This adds the one-line RAII guard at the top of `generate()`. The guard is a nesting-safe thread-local stack and every Keeper-reaching call above is a descendant of that scope, so no deeper placement is needed. Same shape as #113295 for `MergeTreeCodecBlockCountsSource::generate` and the sibling `MergeTreeTextIndexSource::generate`. Of the four callers of `makeTextIndexInputStream`, the other three already have an ancestor guard (`MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate` for both `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` sites, the mutate/merge task guards for `MergeTextIndexesTask`); this step was the only gap. Category is `CI Fix or Improvement`, as in #113295 and #113386: the metadata-in-Keeper storage type is registered only under `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts only in debug and sanitizer builds, so this cannot happen in an official stable build. For the same reason no test is added: no public build reaches Keeper through `existsFile`. Validated with the existing `02346_text_index*` suite (plus 50/50 randomized runs of `02346_text_index_optimize_trivial_count`), an `EXPLAIN` assertion that the modified scope is the one the query executes, and a run with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking = 1`. Left alone: the plan-time `getDeserializedFormat` path can also reach `existsFile` for packed skip-index parts and is likewise unguarded, but it predates this step by three weeks and is not this failure's carrier.

signal.title: Detect column-vs-skip-index stream base collisions when writing a part
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112681 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` and silent data corruption when a column is named into the `skp_idx_` prefix so that its on-disk stream base equals a skip index's, making both share one marks file. Such a write is now rejected with `INCORRECT_FILE_NAME` naming both owners. ### Description `skp_idx_` is a prefix convention, not a reserved namespace, and `escapeForFileName` emits `_` and alphanumerics verbatim. So a column named `skp_idx_a` beside an index `a` claims the same on-disk base, and both writers derive the same marks path from it. At default settings the INSERT fails: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64, `skp_idx_a` UInt64, s String, INDEX a(s) TYPE set(100) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number, toString(number) FROM numbers(10); -- Logical error: 'Incorrect mark rows for part ... in-memory 10, on disk 1, total marks 2' ``` Reaching the same state through a mutation is worse: the carried index files are hardlinked onto the column's base, `CHECK TABLE` reports OK, and only reading the column reveals `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`. `RENAME COLUMN` into such a name fails with a bare `errno 17`. Both namespaces are laid down in one directory by producers with private registries, so neither sees the other: `addStreams` rejects columns-vs-columns but never sees index names. It cannot be decided at DDL time either, since exact stream enumeration needs the chosen serializations, the actual data (Map bucket counts, JSON dynamic paths, Dynamic variants) and the part format, and the last two do not exist yet. So detect it at write time, where the names are already computed. A `StreamBaseManifest` is created once per part-write operation and shared by every producer writing into that directory, reusing the `external_packed_skip_indices_writer` pattern, so no writer or factory signature changes. Producers register the bases they create with their own identity, and a conflicting claim throws; nothing is inferred from a filename. Projections get their own instance, since `<name>.proj/` is its own directory. Compact parts need no check: all their columns share one `data.bin`. A pre-existing table with a colliding pair still ATTACHes; its first write now fails cleanly instead of aborting. Verified in both directions, plus the Sparse, Tuple, Dynamic, hashed, packed, vertical-merge, text-index and mutation carry paths, with negative arms pinning the legal shapes.

signal.title: Show why a job failed when it never uploaded its own report
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113382 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not user-facing: CI report only. ### Description Two jobs on #113382 lost their runner mid-`Run`, and both report pages render nothing, so the failure looks like a 0-second job with no output: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 praktika did detect the failure and record the reason, but three defects hide it. `_finish_workflow` reported such a job only through `env.add_workflow_error(..., source=result.name)`. `source=` sets the `from` label, not the destination, so the message landed on the workflow node while the job's own node kept an empty `info`, and the page renders notifications from the node it resolved, which is the job. The `Status.ERROR` sites in `runner.py` already call `add_error` on the job's own result; this site did not. A job uploads its own `result_<job>.json` from inside the job, so a job that dies never uploads one and S3 answers 403. The page turned that 403 into "Report does not exist or expired" and returned, discarding the workflow report it had already fetched, which does contain the job's node. That early return is gone, and the cached per-job report is now overwritten on every fetch that came back, so a page polling `sha=latest` cannot keep showing an older commit's node. Rendering that node exposed a third defect, already on master: the auto-reload predicate asked whether the per-job report was running, so a null one read as still loading and the page refetched S3 every 30 seconds forever. It now asks the node the page actually renders. The runner loss is not fixable here and this does not try to. A test drives `_finish_workflow` against a stubbed environment and asserts the reason reaches the uploaded workflow report. For the page, a script extracts the relevant functions from `json.html` and replays the measured S3 responses. Reverting any one fix alone reintroduces its symptom; the healthy and expired paths stay byte-identical.

signal.title: Paimon tables with a nullable ARRAY or MAP column cannot be read: "Nested type ... cannot be inside Nullable type"
signal.text: A Paimon table containing a nullable `ARRAY` or `MAP` column cannot be read at all: schema parsing wraps the composite type in `Nullable`, which ClickHouse forbids, so `DESC` and `SELECT` throw an exception before any data is read. Since Paimon columns are nullable by default (e.g. any Spark-created table with an array column), this makes fairly ordinary Paimon tables entirely unreadable — the exception is raised while parsing the table schema in `PaimonMetadata::create`, so it affects the whole table, not just queries touching the offending column. **How to reproduce** Write a Paimon table with a nullable array column (Paimon 1.1.1, Spark 3.5): ```sql -- spark-sql with org.apache.paimon:paimon-spark-3.5:1.1.1, -- spark.sql.catalog.paimon = org.apache.paimon.spark.SparkCatalog, -- spark.sql.catalog.paimon.warehouse = file:/tmp/paimon_wh CREATE TABLE paimon.default.t (f ARRAY<INT>) TBLPROPERTIES ('file.format'='parquet'); INSERT INTO paimon.default.t VALUES (array(1,2)); ``` Read it with ClickHouse (master, commit `7c826d816cd5`): ``` $ clickhouse local --query "DESC paimonLocal('/tmp/paimon_wh/default.db/t')" Code: 43. DB::Exception: Nested type Array(Nullable(Int32)) cannot be inside Nullable type. (ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT) ``` The same error occurs via `paimonS3` / `paimonAzure` and the `Paimon*` table engines. A nullable `MAP` column fails identically with `Nested type Map(...) cannot be inside Nullable type`. **Root cause** `Paimon::DataType::parse` in `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h` wraps the result in `DataTypeNullable` when the Paimon field is nullable, including for the `ARRAY` and `MAP` branches: ```cpp if (real_type == "ARRAY") { ... type.clickhouse_data_type = std::make_shared<DataTypeArray>(nested_type.clickhouse_data_type); if (nullable) type.clickhouse_data_type = std::make_shared<DataTypeNullable>(type.clickhouse_data_type); } ``` `DataTypeNullable`'s constructor rejects composite nested types (`src/DataTypes/DataTypeNullable.cpp`), hence the exception. The `Nullable` wrap should be skipped for `ARRAY` and `MAP` (reading a null array/map as empty), which is how the Iceberg and Delta Lake type mappers handle nullable composites. The existing test fixtures (`tests/queries/0_stateless/data_minio/paimon_all_types`) never hit this because their array/map fields are declared non-nullable. The new Paimon type-matrix E2E test works around it with `NOT NULL` composite columns for now. Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/102343 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #113450 - Backported to: `26.7.4.30`, `26.6.3.39`, `26.5.7.51` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Buffer table silently discards an acknowledged INSERT when the destination schema drifts (DROP / re-CREATE) before the deferred flush
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse QA (durability testing) ### Describe what's wrong An `INSERT` into a `Buffer` table is acknowledged as soon as the rows land in the in-memory buffer; the write to the destination table happens later (background threshold flush, or `OPTIMIZE`). If the destination's schema *diverges* in that window, the flush silently discards the acknowledged rows and reports success — the client that received the `INSERT` acknowledgement never sees any error. Two variants lose whole acked rows during normal, server-healthy operation: - the destination is dropped and re-created with a column set that has **no name in common** with the buffer → the whole buffered block is discarded; - the destination is **dropped** (a migration step) before the flush fires → the whole buffered block is discarded. `StorageBuffer::writeBlockToDestination` logs these two cases at `<Error>` level — i.e. the code treats them as error conditions — but then `return`s normally, so `flushBuffer` counts the flush as successful and clears the buffer (`src/Storages/StorageBuffer.cpp:1085-1089` for the missing-destination case, `:1120-1124` for the no-common-columns case). Only a thrown exception restores the block to the buffer, so the rows are gone from everywhere with only a server-log line. A third, milder variant is documented (a dropped destination column silently drops that column's acknowledged values while the rows survive — `StorageBuffer.cpp:1103-1127`; documented at `docs/en/engines/table-engines/special/buffer.md`), so this report is about the two **whole-block** losses, which the docs do not cover. This is the same durability class as #112394 (Buffer losing buffered rows on graceful shutdown), but a distinct mechanism: here the server stays up and healthy, and the trigger is an ordinary destination schema change (`DROP`/re-`CREATE`/`ALTER`) between the acknowledgement and the deferred flush. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduces on 26.8.1.1. `StorageBuffer::writeBlockToDestination` carries the same discard-with-log logic on current `master`. ### How to reproduce `clickhouse-server` 26.8.1.1, single node, default settings. ```sql CREATE TABLE dst (k UInt64, v String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; -- Buffer thresholds set high so no auto-flush fires before the drift; a -- production Buffer with ordinary thresholds hits the same discard on its -- background flush. CREATE TABLE buf AS dst ENGINE = Buffer(currentDatabase(), 'dst', 1, 3600, 7200, 1000000, 2000000, 100000000, 200000000); INSERT INTO buf SELECT number, concat('payload_', toString(number)) FROM numbers(50); -- The INSERT is acknowledged. The rows are visible through the buffer: SELECT count() FROM buf; -- 50 SELECT count() FROM dst; -- 0 (not flushed yet) -- An ordinary destination migration: drop and re-create with a different schema. DROP TABLE dst; CREATE TABLE dst (a UInt64, b String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; OPTIMIZE TABLE buf; -- flush; returns success SELECT count() FROM dst; -- 0 -> the 50 acknowledged rows are gone ``` The whole-block loss also reproduces when the destination is simply dropped and not re-created before the flush. ### Expected behavior An acknowledged `INSERT` should not be silently lost while the server is healthy. At minimum the flush should not report success when it discards an acknowledged block: the discard is already recognized as an error internally (it is logged at `<Error>`), so it should surface to a place the client or an operator can observe (an exception that keeps the block buffered and retries, or a failure counter / `system.errors` entry), rather than clearing the buffer and returning success. ### Error message and/or stacktrace Server log only; nothing is returned to the client. From a run of the reproduction: ``` <Error> StorageBuffer (default.buf): Destination table default.dst have no common columns with block in buffer. Block of data is discarded. <Error> StorageBuffer (default.buf): Destination table default.dst doesn't exist. Block of data is discarded. ``` ### Additional context Reproduced 5/5 with a non-vacuity control (no drift → all 50 rows flush) and the acknowledged rows proven present through the buffer before the drift. Code references are against `master` at `aa3ccbf5e7df`.

signal.title: S3 multipart complete: a NoSuchUpload is rewritten to success on key existence alone, silently losing an acknowledged fixed-key INSERT
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse QA (durability testing) ### Describe what's wrong When an S3 `CompleteMultipartUpload` returns `NoSuchUpload`, `DB::S3::Client::CompleteMultipartUpload` disambiguates by **key existence only**: it issues a `HeadObject` on the target key and, if any object exists there, rewrites the outcome to a fabricated success — with no upload-id, ETag, size, or version cross-check against the upload that just failed (`src/IO/S3/Client.cpp:531-551`): ```cpp if (!outcome.IsSuccess() && outcome.GetError().GetErrorType() == Aws::S3::S3Errors::NO_SUCH_UPLOAD) { auto check_request = HeadObjectRequest().WithBucket(bucket).WithKey(key); auto check_outcome = HeadObject(check_request); /// if the key exists, than MultipartUpload has been completed at some of the retries /// rewrite outcome with success status if (check_outcome.IsSuccess()) outcome = Aws::S3::Model::CompleteMultipartUploadOutcome(Aws::S3::Model::CompleteMultipartUploadResult()); } ``` The rewrite is meant for the benign retry-idempotency case (a lost complete response where an earlier attempt already completed). But key existence is not proof that *this* upload completed. If the target is a **fixed key that already holds a prior object** (an overwrite via `s3_truncate_on_insert = 1`, or a foreign writer) and this multipart upload was genuinely aborted between create and complete — e.g. by an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` bucket lifecycle rule (a widely recommended, common configuration) racing a slow/large INSERT, or by a concurrent abort — then `CompleteMultipartUpload` legitimately returns `NoSuchUpload`, the `HeadObject` finds the **prior** object, the outcome is rewritten to success, and the INSERT is **acknowledged while zero of its rows are durable**. The old object is served forever; the client sees no error. The secondary guard `check_objects_after_upload` is off by default (`src/IO/S3Defines.h`) and even when on it checks key existence + size only. Scope: fixed-key writes — `s3()` / `S3` engine, especially with `s3_truncate_on_insert = 1`. MergeTree-over-S3 uses unique random keys, so a `HeadObject` there fails and the error propagates correctly (no loss). Distinct from #112419 (two concurrent same-key INSERTs) and #113179 (local metadata rewrite). ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduces on 26.8.1.1. `Client::CompleteMultipartUpload` carries the same key-only rewrite on current `master`. ### How to reproduce `clickhouse-server` 26.8.1.1 against an S3 endpoint (MinIO), default settings. A fault proxy in front of the endpoint fails the `CompleteMultipartUpload` (POST with `uploadId=`) once with `NoSuchUpload`, **without forwarding** it — so the upload stays genuinely incomplete and the prior object at the key survives (the faithful stand-in for a lifecycle-aborted upload). ```sql -- 1. Seed a small OLD object at the fixed key (single PUT): INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://.../bucket/mpu/obj.csv', 'CSV', 'tag String, filler String') SETTINGS s3_truncate_on_insert = 1 SELECT 'OLD', repeat('x', 50) FROM numbers(100); -- 2. Arm the proxy to fail the next CompleteMultipartUpload with NoSuchUpload -- (unforwarded), then INSERT a LARGE NEW object to the SAME key. The size -- (>32 MiB, the default s3_max_single_part_upload_size) forces a multipart -- upload, so CompleteMultipartUpload is called: INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://.../bucket/mpu/obj.csv', 'CSV', 'tag String, filler String') SETTINGS s3_truncate_on_insert = 1 SELECT 'NEW', repeat('x', 50) FROM numbers(900000); -- ^ returns SUCCESS -- 3. Read the key back: SELECT countIf(tag = 'NEW'), countIf(tag = 'OLD') FROM s3('http://.../bucket/mpu/obj.csv', 'CSV', 'tag String, filler String'); -- 0 100 -> the acknowledged NEW rows are gone; the OLD object is served ``` Control (no fault): the same large NEW INSERT lands the 900000 NEW rows and 0 OLD — the multipart write path and truncate work; the loss is caused by the rewrite. ### Expected behavior An acknowledged INSERT must not be silently lost. When `CompleteMultipartUpload` returns `NoSuchUpload`, the `HeadObject` disambiguation should confirm the object at the key is *this* upload's result before rewriting to success — e.g. compare the ETag against the multipart tags already known to the writer, or the object size against the total written, rather than treating mere key existence as proof. If it cannot be confirmed, the complete should fail (so the INSERT errors and can be retried), not be reported as success. ### Error message and/or stacktrace None — the INSERT returns success. The only trace is that a later read of the key returns the pre-existing object's content instead of the inserted rows. ### Additional context Reproduced **5/5** with a non-vacuity control (no fault → the NEW object lands) and the INSERT acknowledged (`rc = 0`) in every faulted iteration. Code references are against `master` at `aa3ccbf5e7df`.
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: INSERT on a DDL-lagging Replicated-database replica silently skips an un-applied materialized view's cascade, permanently losing the acknowledged rows from the MV target
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse QA (durability testing) ### Describe what's wrong An `INSERT` into a table inside a `Replicated` database is acknowledged by the replica that receives it, and that replica alone fires the source table's materialized-view cascade. It captures the set of dependent views from its **local** catalog (`DatabaseCatalog::getDependentViews`). If that replica is **behind on the Replicated-database DDL log** and has not yet applied a `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` entry, its local catalog has no MV — so the acknowledged `INSERT` writes only the source table, and the MV target table never receives the rows. This is permanent: after the DDL log catches up and the MV is created on that replica, the earlier acknowledged rows are **not** back-filled. The client that received the `INSERT` acknowledgement sees no error. The streaming-ingestion path guards exactly this situation. `DatabaseCatalog::getReadyDependentViews` (`src/Interpreters/DatabaseCatalog.cpp:1148`) returns an empty set — refusing to process — when the dependency graph is only partially loaded, with the comment *"Return empty to prevent streaming engines from processing with a partial dependency graph, which would permanently lose data for views not yet loaded."* The plain-`INSERT` path does not use that guard: `InsertDependenciesBuilder` reads the unguarded `getDependentViews` (`src/Interpreters/InsertDependenciesBuilder.cpp:898` and `:984`). So a Kafka/S3Queue/RabbitMQ consumer with a not-yet-loaded view is held back, but a plain `INSERT` on the same replica proceeds and silently drops the cascade. The realistic trigger is a replica that is recovering / catching up on the Replicated-database DDL log (the `unsynced_after_recovery` window, `src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:630`) while already answering queries, and a client that inserts into an existing source table on it — for example a direct connection, or a load balancer that has not yet drained the lagging replica. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — reproduces on 26.8.1.1, and the code path is identical on current `master` (`0eb5eba20b92`). ### How to reproduce Two-replica `Replicated` database on one Keeper. The DDL lag is made deterministic with the `PAUSEABLE` failpoint `database_replicated_stop_entry_execution` (`src/Databases/DatabaseReplicatedWorker.cpp:628`), which pauses a replica's DDL worker in `initAndCheckTask` before it executes the next log entry — so the replica is held with the source and target tables applied but the `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` entry pending. (The failpoint only makes the window exact; the same loss occurs whenever a replica genuinely lags on that DDL entry while taking inserts.) ```sql -- On both replicas r1 and r2: CREATE DATABASE rdb ENGINE = Replicated('/clickhouse/rdb', 's1', 'r1'); -- 'r2' on the other -- Applied on both replicas (before the hold): CREATE TABLE rdb.src (id UInt64, v UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE rdb.dst (id UInt64, v UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree ORDER BY id; -- Hold r2's DDL worker on the NEXT entry (the CREATE MV): -- (on r2) SYSTEM ENABLE FAILPOINT database_replicated_stop_entry_execution; -- On r1: create the MV. r1 applies it; r2 is paused on the entry, so r2 has no MV. CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW rdb.mv TO rdb.dst AS SELECT id, v FROM rdb.src; -- Direct an INSERT at the lagging replica r2 (which has src but not mv): INSERT INTO rdb.src VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30); -- acknowledged SELECT count() FROM rdb.src; -- 3 on both replicas (RMT replication) SELECT count() FROM rdb.dst; -- 0 -> the acknowledged rows never reached the MV target -- Release r2's DDL worker so it finally creates the MV: -- (on r2) SYSTEM DISABLE FAILPOINT database_replicated_stop_entry_execution; SELECT count() FROM rdb.dst; -- still 0 -> no back-fill; the rows are gone from the MV target ``` Observed with the reproduction rig, 5/5 runs, both controls green: - **bug** — r2 held on the CREATE MV entry, INSERT directed at r2: INSERT acknowledged, `src` = 30 on both replicas, `dst` = 0 on both replicas before and after releasing the hold. - **non-vacuity control** — no hold, INSERT on r2 after r2 has the MV: `dst` = 30 (the cascade fires). - **positive control** — r2 held, INSERT directed at r1 (which has the MV): `dst` = 30 (the cascade fires on the receiving replica). ### Expected behavior An acknowledged `INSERT` should not silently skip a materialized view whose `CREATE` has already been committed to the Replicated-database DDL log. The plain-`INSERT` cascade path should apply the same partial-dependency-graph protection the streaming path already has (`getReadyDependentViews`): if the receiving replica has not yet loaded a dependent view that the DDL log says exists, the `INSERT` should be delayed until the view is loaded, or fail loudly, rather than being acknowledged with the cascade silently dropped. ### Error message and/or stacktrace None — the `INSERT` is acknowledged and no error is logged; the rows are simply absent from the MV target. ### Additional context Distinct from #111935 (recovery *drops MV inner-table data*) and #111818 (refreshable-MV records refresh success before durability): here the server is healthy, the MV target is an ordinary explicit table, and the trigger is an ordinary DDL-log lag between the acknowledged `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` and a replica that receives an `INSERT` before applying it. Code references are against `master` at `0eb5eba20b92`.
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: Failed INSERT INTO s3(...) PARTITION BY leaves a durable read-visible prefix; default hive strategy silently duplicates it on retry
signal.text: ### Company or project name ClickHouse QA (durability testing) ### Describe what's wrong A failed `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...) PARTITION BY <key>` (and the equivalent object-storage table engines) is **not atomic and leaves a durable, read-visible prefix of the partitions it had already written**, while the statement reports failure. `PartitionedSink` finalizes one object per partition value **sequentially**, with no rollback of the partitions committed before the one that fails: ```cpp // src/Storages/PartitionedSink.cpp:120-125 void PartitionedSink::onFinish() { for (auto & [_, sink] : partition_id_to_sink) { sink->onFinish(); // each StorageObjectStorageSink::onFinish -> finalizeBuffers -> write_buf->finalize() (the durable PUT / CompleteMultipartUpload) } } ``` Each child `StorageObjectStorageSink::onFinish` (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:89-119`) finalizes (PUTs) its own object. If the PUT of partition *k* throws, the exception propagates out of the loop; the partitions finalized **before** *k* are already durable and immediately listable/readable, and nothing deletes them or records that only a prefix landed (`cancelBuffers` only aborts the not-yet-finalized buffers). So the error's implied "nothing happened" contract is a lie. The consequence on the **default** partition strategy is silent duplication on a natural retry. `file_like_engine_default_partition_strategy` defaults to `HIVE` (`src/Core/Settings.cpp:7754`), and `HiveStylePartitionStrategy::getPathForWrite` appends a fresh `generateSnowflakeID()` to every filename: ```cpp // src/Storages/IPartitionStrategy.cpp:383 path += std::to_string(generateSnowflakeID()) + "." + Poco::toLower(file_format); ``` so every attempt writes new object keys. A client that treats the failed INSERT as "nothing happened" and re-submits it therefore **duplicates every partition that survived the first attempt** — there is no dedup for object-storage writes and no exists-check that can catch it (the keys differ each time). A client that does *not* re-submit is left with silently half-applied state. The `WILDCARD` strategy (an explicit `{_partition_id}` placeholder in the path) fails safe instead of duplicating: the retry recomputes the same keys and the exists-check rejects it (`Code: 36 ... already exists, enable s3_truncate_on_insert`), which is fail-closed but still leaves the client permanently half-applied and unable to tell which partitions survived without listing the bucket. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — reproduced deterministically on 26.8.1.1. The code paths (`PartitionedSink::onFinish`, `StorageObjectStorageSink::finalizeBuffers`, `HiveStylePartitionStrategy::getPathForWrite`, and the `HIVE` default) are all present on current `master`. ### How to reproduce A durability rig reproduces both facets 3/3 with controls (MinIO behind a fault proxy that returns a non-retryable `403 AccessDenied` on **one** partition's PUT — the classic least-privilege / transient-denial to a single prefix — and a single clean server). `N = 300` rows over 3 partition values `p = number % 3`. **Facet 1 — a failed INSERT leaves a read-visible prefix (WILDCARD path, deterministic):** 1. `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://.../base/{_partition_id}/data.parquet', ..., 'Parquet', 'id UInt64, p UInt64') PARTITION BY p SELECT number AS id, number % 3 AS p FROM numbers(300)`, with the proxy denying PUTs to the key of the partition that finalizes **last**. 2. The INSERT fails (`Code: 499 ... S3_ERROR`), yet the two partitions finalized before it are durable and queryable through the object store, while the faulted partition is absent. - **Clean control** (proxy disarmed): the 3-partition INSERT round-trips all 300 rows. - **Isolation control** (same fault, but `INSERT ... PARTITION BY p ... WHERE p = <faulted>` — a single partition, no fan-out): the INSERT fails and **nothing** is durable, proving the surviving prefix in step 2 is the fan-out's doing. **Facet 2 — the default HIVE strategy silently duplicates on retry:** 1. Same INSERT into a non-wildcard path (default `partition_strategy = hive`), denying PUTs to one partition's `p=<v>/` prefix. 2. The INSERT fails; a `SELECT count()` over the whole prefix returns **200** (the two surviving partitions). 3. The client re-submits the identical INSERT (its natural response to a failed op). It succeeds, and `SELECT count()` over the prefix now returns **500** — 300 unique rows plus the **200-row surviving prefix duplicated** (fresh snowflake filenames, no dedup, no exists-check). ### Expected behavior A failed `INSERT ... PARTITION BY` should not silently leave a durable, read-visible subset of its partitions with the statement reporting failure. Either the partitioned write should roll back the partitions it already committed on failure (so the error's "nothing happened" contract holds), or the surviving prefix should be recorded/surfaced so the outcome is not silently half-applied — and in particular, on the **default** hive strategy a natural client retry of a failed partitioned INSERT should not silently duplicate the rows of the partitions that survived the first attempt. Honest caveat: object-storage writes through the `s3`/`azureBlobStorage` table functions and engines are not transactional, and at-least-once export is a known property. What this report isolates is the specific, undocumented combination — a failed multi-partition INSERT leaves a **query-visible** durable prefix, and the **default** hive strategy makes an ordinary retry duplicate that prefix with no dedup and no way to be idempotent — which is a data-integrity footgun distinct from the concurrent-writer clobber already filed as #112419. ### Error message and/or stacktrace `Code: 499. DB::Exception: ... (S3_ERROR)` on the faulted INSERT; `Code: 36 ... Object in bucket ... already exists (...enable s3_truncate_on_insert)` on the wildcard retry.

signal.title: Data loss with ATTACH PARTITION ... ON CLUSTER in ReplicatedMergeTree
signal.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong We are running a 2-shard bare-metal cluster: - Shard 1: 2 replicas (ReplicatedMergeTree) - Shard 2: 1 replica (single node with no replication) We use a staging-to-target table pattern for our ETL, following the official [ClickLoad guidelines](https://clickhouse.com/blog/supercharge-your-clickhouse-data-loads-part3) which suggest using ON CLUSTER for sharded clusters: "The [MOVE PARTITION operations](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickLoad/blob/main/src/worker.py#L592) must run on all shards in a sharded cluster, e.g., by utilizing the [ON CLUSTER](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/sql-reference/distributed-ddl) clause" We found a critical issue where about half of our data disappears / goes missing if we run the ATTACH PARTITION command using ON CLUSTER. `ALTER TABLE target_local ATTACH PARTITION 202608 FROM staging_local ON CLUSTER 'my_cluster';` ### The Issue: - When we run this query with `ON CLUSTER`, it executes on all replicas concurrently. - The result is **massive data loss.** The target table ends up with only about half of the expected row count, and the rest of the data seems to vanish (some parts might end up stuck or lost during the concurrent move). ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce ClickHouse Version: 26.3.12.3 (or any recent stable version) Cluster topology: Sharded cluster with ReplicatedMergeTree (at least 2 replicas on one of the shards). Steps: 1. Load a large volume of data into a staging table (generating a high number of active data parts). 2. Execute the partition promotion using ON CLUSTER: `ALTER TABLE target_local ATTACH PARTITION 202608 FROM staging_local ON CLUSTER 'my_cluster';` 3. Under high part count and concurrency, this triggers write conflicts in ZooKeeper. ### Expected behavior The partition should attach successfully on all replicas without data loss. The ON CLUSTER coordination should safely execute the ATTACH on a single replica per shard and let standard replication handle the rest, rather than having all replicas concurrently attempt ZooKeeper registration. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context ### My Questions: 1. Why does running ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM ... ON CLUSTER cause data loss on ReplicatedMergeTree tables? Is this a known bug or a race condition with ZooKeeper? 2. Is there any way to safely use ON CLUSTER for this staging pattern without risking data deletion/loss? 3. Is external orchestration (e.g., triggering the DDL locally on exactly one replica per shard) the officially recommended way to handle this on bare-metal deployments?
